Junk bonds are 'flashing yellow.' Watch these warning signs

📅 09 Oct 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (1025 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: CNBC

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Cracks are forming in the junk bond market as investors demand higher payouts for owning the market's riskiest debt.
  • High-yield bonds now yield 8.1%, up from 7.22% a month ago.
  • In a recent development, the high-yield market is also showing stress on the credit side with spreads recently widening to levels not seen since April, according to the Federal Reserve Bank of St.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Cracks are forming in the junk bond market as investors demand higher payouts for owning the market's riskiest debt. It isn't time to ditch high-yield bonds, but investors should pay attention to the warning signs.

High-yield bonds now yield 8.1%, up from 7.22% a month ago. The increase reflects a jump in yields across the curve as investors bake in more inflation from high energy prices and other pressures, including concern about the deficit — hitting nearly $2 trillion in the fiscal year that ended Sept. 30.

In a recent development, the high-yield market is also showing stress on the credit side with spreads recently widening to levels not seen since April, according to the Federal Reserve Bank of St. Louis. Credit spreads are the difference in yield between the bonds and Treasurys of similar maturities. Wider spreads mean investors are demanding higher yields for holding corporate debt, viewing it as riskier.

In a recent development, spreads are at 315 basis points in the overall high-yield market, higher than a year ago but still below levels in March when they reached 346 bps. One basis point equals one one-hundredth of a percent, or 0.01%.

Sources indicate that the high-yield market consists of bonds rated BB+ by S&P and Fitch and Ba1 and under by Moody's. The lowest-rated cohort, CCC and below, has seen the most movement with spreads climbing dramatically over the past year to roughly 1,250 bps.

Right now, the high-yield market is "flashing yellow" but is "far from red," said Michael Arone, chief investment strategist at State Street Investment Management.

It makes sense that investors are demanding more compensation for taking on additional credit risk as borrowing costs rise, he stated.

Yields are elevated across the board with the 10-year Treasury reaching its highest level since 2002 earlier in the week.

"The bigger question is whether this is simply a repricing of interest rate risk, or the beginning of a more fundamental reassessment of credit quality," Arone mentioned.

He's in a wait-and-see mode since earnings are still growing, interest-coverage ratios remain good, and while default rates have ticked up some, he believes it is not concerning.

That said, the starting point in spreads is likely weighing on investors' psyche, since they are still low by historical standards.

According to recent reports, "There's a small margin of error here, which I also think raises the anxiety level," Arone explained. "The compensation that investors are receiving for taking on this credit risk isn't overwhelming relative to history, and therefore subtle changes in credit spreads can be concerning.".

While there may be concerns about part of the lower-rated market, the overall high-yield market is in good fundamental shape.

In fact, credit quality is at a record high, with BB bonds making up over 60% of the market compared with 38% prior to the global financial crisis, mentioned Kelley Gerrity, a fixed income strategist at Morgan Stanley Investment Management.

In a recent development, "We've had higher-quality companies coming in, and with higher rates now, you also have more discipline from companies that are more indebted ... just because of the higher cost of capital, so that actually is creating a bit of a healthier picture as well," she stated.

The lowest tier of high yield has always been more speculative, since the bonds have a higher default risk. Therefore, it's no surprise that they are the ones seeing the most widening in spreads, noted Collin Martin, head of fixed income research and strategy at the Schwab Center for Financial Research.

The overall move in high-yield spreads have been "orderly," he said. "Are there cracks forming? I think the cracks are logical cracks with the lowest-rated bonds and it's too early to say that it's spreading to the broad credit market.".

In a recent development, in addition, fluctuations within the CCC-rated and lower spreads have been idiosyncratic, Gerrity added. Morgan Stanley recently broke down the spreads in the lowest cohort into two buckets: performing assets and non-performing assets, which are defined as spreads above 1,000 bps.

The non-performing spread to worst is 2,818 bps, while the performing bucket — the biggest piece of the CCC market — is 461 bps, she said.

It has been revealed that "It is isolated," she mentioned. "I'm not necessarily sure that that will go away anytime soon, but it doesn't tell the story of overall concern and flashing caution for credit markets right now.".

For now, investors should remain selective within higher yield, Gerrity advised.

"We're looking for the best relative value opportunities, and we think that exists within that single-B cohort, and so we're leaning into that," she remarked.

Investors should be concerned if there is a steep widening in the broader high-yield market.

But there's scant evidence of stress in the BB cohort. Spreads in that group are at 194 bps, up from 179 bps a year ago — although the move hasn't been in a straight line.

"We're going to be focusing our attention on what are considered some stronger businesses," Martin mentioned. "If we start to see the markets demand higher spreads there also, that's what we'll be looking at to see if risks are really rising.".

It's also key to understand that the Federal Reserve is raising rates in a strong economic environment, mentioned R.J. Gallo, chief investment officer of global fixed income at Federated Hermes. The central bank is concerned about an inflation problem amid high fossil fuel prices due to the Iran war, while growth has been stronger than expected, he noted.

"With growth being good as the reason that the Fed is hiking, then you wouldn't expect high yield to blow out because growth means revenues stay up, means cash flow and profitability stays up," he explained.

High yield becomes a disaster when the economy is heading into a sharp economic downturn, Gallo said.

"That's when spreads really widen out," he mentioned. "But a recession is not the odds-on bet. Now, talk to me in six months if the Fed keeps hiking over and over, if oil prices stay high for longer, well, then maybe we will start to wonder.".

💡 Key Takeaways

  • With that as the backdrop, while bigger companies like Apple (AAPL +1.90%), Nvidia (NVDA +31.48%), and Microsoft (MSFT +1.65%) technically have the bigger, better numbers right now to justify their bigger market capitalizations, I've got a feeling that within five years, Google parent Alphabet (GOOG +5.88%) (GOOGL +6.34%) will be the world's most valuable organization.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By James Brumley – Nov 24, 2026 at 3:50AM EST.

10 stocks we like better than Alphabet ›.

Investors love numbers, understandably so. Numerical data is how we measure a organization's success, or gauge the value of the market, or, for that matter, decide the health of the economy.

Sometimes, though, it can be helpful to consider qualitative information at least as much as the quantitative for a particular organization (Warren Buffett does!) when making a buy/sell decision.

With that as the backdrop, while bigger companies like Apple (AAPL +1.90%), Nvidia (NVDA +31.48%), and Microsoft (MSFT +1.65%) technically have the bigger, better numbers right now to justify their bigger market capitalizations, I've got a feeling that within five years, Google parent Alphabet (GOOG +5.88%) (GOOGL +6.34%) will be the world's most valuable organization. Here's why.

Industry observers note that don't misunderstand. All of these organizations are likely to continue growing between now and 2031, with each apt to have larger market caps by the end of this time frame. Alphabet is simply set to outpace their growth.

Sources indicate that take Apple as an example. Although last fiscal year's top-line growth of 15% is robust to be sure, the iPhone continues to account for half of its revenue. That's a potential problem simply because the smartphone market itself may be peaking due to sheer saturation.

Recent findings suggest that while high memory prices have crimped smartphone demand this year, even before this year's cost pressures, IDC reports that smartphone unit sales improved by less than 2% last year. Although Apple technically led that growth, it did so with a year-over-year improvement of a mere 6.3%.

Indeed, according to figures from Omdia and Counterpoint Research, smartphone sales (measured in units) peaked in 2014. The bulk of the business's growth since then -- including Apple's -- just reflects higher prices, which technically drive growth but aren't a sustainable long-term growth proposal. And again, the iPhone still makes up roughly half of Apple's business.

As for Nvidia, the world will still need plenty of processing chips between now and 2031, artificial intelligence chips in particular. The company's revenue soared 103% year over year last quarter, driven by insatiable demand for AI accelerators.

Industry observers note that this need will eventually be fully met; however, it will largely limit the market to replacements and upgrades rather than demand for entirely new AI platforms. In this vein, for perspective, industry research outfit SemiAnalysis recently reduced its 2028 forecast for AI chip sales from just over $1 trillion to $758 billion, while dialing back its 2030 outlook from just over $1.5 trillion to $923 billion.

And as for Microsoft, while it hasn't been a leading player in the artificial intelligence movement thus far, its woes began well before the AI revolution took hold. Although it's still a powerhouse software name to be sure (with ongoing revenue growth to prove it), the personal computer market peaked in 2011, undermining Windows as a sales tool for other, newer Microsoft products. Indeed, there are now more mobile devices running Android than desktops running Windows, according to Statcounter, and this divergence may only widen going forward.

In a recent development, alphabet owns Android, of course, which, by the way, also dominates the mobile OS market with a 72% share. Android isn't a stand-alone profit center, however. It's free for consumers.

In a recent development, rather, Android's domination of the mobile operating system market positions it as a de facto gatekeeper -- and tollbooth operator of sorts -- for how most consumers now prefer to navigate the worldwide web. Numbers from Manochi indicate 52.6% of the planet's web traffic now originates from smartphones.

According to recent reports, and regardless of where it came from, Statcounter reports that Alphabet's Google still handles 91% of the world's web searches, with each one of these billions of daily search queries being worth a few cents. For many people, the Google name and platform and the name have become nearly synonymous with the internet itself.

NASDAQ · As of 4:00 PM ET 11/23/26.

This doesn't mean Alphabet's always done as well with Google as some investors might have hoped. It does, however, mean the company's got lots of options for monetizing its role as a gateway to the worldwide web. This flexibility is an important strategic advantage in and of itself, and the business itself clearly isn't going away anytime soon, even if some of it migrates toward AI chatbots like ChatGPT and Google's Gemini.

Industry observers note that the 800-pound gorilla in the room is, of course, Alphabet's cloud computing operation, which includes artificial intelligence initiatives like the aforementioned Gemini and hardware such as its Tensor Processing Units (TPUs). While not Alphabet's biggest business in terms of total revenue, up 103% to $30.78 billion in the third quarter, it is the company's fastest-growing one.

Industry observers note that and this number merits mentioning: Cloud computing rivals Amazon (AMZN +3.47%) -- via Amazon Web Services, or AWS -- and Microsoft aren't seeing nearly as much growth as Google Cloud is at this time. Both are losing market share.

According to recent reports, image source: Synergy Research Group. Chart by author.

What gives? It's a bit philosophical, but whereas Amazon and Microsoft sell AI services, Google Cloud offers complete turnkey AI solutions, including integration with its powerful TPUs, along with all the software and apps that make the most of their capabilities.

Sources indicate that this is a competitive edge too. Although the entire artificial intelligence industry's growth should slow over the next five years, it's also likely to evolve in ways that funnel customers to providers like Google, which can offer complete one-stop solutions.

Recent findings suggest that so it's conceivable that Alphabet ends up winning the lion's share of whatever growth the AI business has left in store between now and 2031. It's not clear that Nvidia, Amazon, or Microsoft are as well positioned.

That's the prediction anyway. Just remember that it doesn't necessarily mean the market's more valuable companies right now will perform poorly in the meantime.

By Marc Guberti – Nov 24, 2026 at 3:55AM EST.

10 stocks we like better than Unity Software ›.

Unity Software (U +6.10%) might surprise a lot of investors in 2027. A multi-year pivot to adtech is finally bearing fruit. Although the stock has lost more than 70% of its value over the past five years, investors are betting on a rebound as fundamentals finally catch up to the transformation.

Unity's Vector infrastructure uses AI to display ads to people who are more likely to click them. It's a similar model to the one that AppLovin (APP +7.36%) uses, which resulted in that growth stock roughly quadrupling over the past five years. This part of the business is already experiencing substantial growth.

NYSE · As of 4:00 PM ET 11/23/26.

According to recent reports, vector revenue surged by 126% year over year, and that included a 40% sequential jump. Unity's leadership has talked about this day for a while, but it's finally here, and Vector even powered Unity to its first GAAP profitable quarter since its IPO.

Unity CEO Matt Bromberg highlighted the flywheel effect that's taking place. More developers create games on Unity's platforms, and those extra games lead to more online ads.

According to recent reports, although Unity reported 126% year-over-year growth from its Vector segment, its overall revenue was only up by 32% year over year. Looking into this further paints a much brighter outlook as legacy businesses fade away.

Industry observers note that for instance, Unity's non-strategic revenue dropped by 73% year over year to $25.5 million. This part of the business primarily consists of a former advertising network that was sunset in the second quarter, along with its Supersonic business, which was sold off on Aug. 4, 2026.

Non-strategic revenue is only projected to reach $5 million in the fourth quarter and will soon vanish from the income statement. Strategic Revenue, which represents Unity's future, was up by 59% year over year.

It actually gets even better when you look deeper into Strategic Revenue, since it consists of two parts. The Strategic Create Revenue is the smaller segment, and it was up by 11% year over year. Unity projects a 4% to 6% growth rate for this segment in Q4.

Strategic Grow Revenue, which includes Vector, was up by 90% year over year. It's projected to reach $520 million at the high end of Q4 guidance, implying a 20.5% sequential boost and 106% year-over-year growth.

Recent findings suggest that as non-strategic revenue vanishes and growth segments continue to ramp up and make up a larger percentage of total revenue, Unity should continue to post elevated growth rates in the upcoming quarters. Unity also pivoted from a -27% net profit margin in third-quarter 2025 to a 20% positive net profit margin in Q3 2026.

The significant switch to profitability and soaring margins suggest that Unity's net income will grow promptly alongside its Vector advertising infrastructure.

Dreading Holiday Money Talks With Family? Here's What to Say

📅 23 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (811 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Nerdwallet

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Holiday gatherings have a way of stirring up difficult and downright uncomfortable conversations — and not just about politics or cousin Derek’s love life.
  • Industry observers note that relatives and friends may also bring up their money troubles and financial prepares.
  • It’s easy to feel obligated or pressured to help out.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Holiday gatherings have a way of stirring up difficult and downright uncomfortable conversations — and not just about politics or cousin Derek’s love life.

Industry observers note that relatives and friends may also bring up their money troubles and financial prepares. That might involve asking you to lend money or your credit.

It’s easy to feel obligated or pressured to help out. But it’s notable to establish boundaries so you don’t end up making a decision you’ll regret.

If you suspect a money request is coming your way, think carefully about what you’re willing — and able — to offer. You might choose a specific dollar limit or to give no financial help at all.

“Only lend what you're truly OK losing,” states Alvin Carlos, a certified financial planner at District Capital Management in Washington, D.C. “Look at your budget and decide what you could hand over and never see again.”.

Choose the language that best fits your situation. Adapt your responses as needed to guide the conversation in a direction that works for you.

Sources indicate that “I understand that you need help. I just need to review my own finances before I can give you an answer. I’ll get back to you by [day].”.

If the request comes up at a holiday or family gathering:.

“I’d rather discuss this privately. Let’s find another time to talk.”.

“Here's what I’m comfortable with, and here's what I have to protect to be financially safe, mentally safe, and to continue to be there for you in the ways that you need me.”Or, if you want to be more direct:.

Sometimes, there’s an unspoken expectation to give money because of how much loved ones think you earn, indicates Ashley Agnew, a certified financial therapist in Boston.

Getting ahead of it before there's a tipping point can help with tricky dynamics, she indicates.

A recent Edward Jones report found that only about one-third of financial caregiving arrangements were planned and discussed in advance. The report also found that nearly half of financial caregivers (49%) make financial sacrifices, such as reducing or stopping saving, or tapping into their retirement account.

Factor your financial health, your values and emotional well-being into your decision:.

It has been revealed that review your income, expenses and savings. If you provide financial help and don’t get the money back, would you struggle to pay bills or reach financial goals? Prioritize building an emergency fund, saving for retirement and paying off high-interest debt first, Carlos says.

Consider your relationship. Would you feel resentful if you aren’t repaid? How do you think your friend or relative would react if you decline to help? Could it damage your relationship, and if so, is it worth it?

Understand the credit risks. Co-signing or allowing someone else to use your credit can leave you responsible for payments and expose you to potential credit damage.

Sources indicate that know the tax implications. If you’re considering a substantial gift or loan, check with a tax professional about any reporting requirements and tax consequences.

In a recent development, consult your partner. If you share finances, make sure to include your partner in your decision-making process, Agnew says. If you have a parent asking for financial assistance, for example, but your cultural view is different from your spouse's, that’s a big opportunity for a rift.

Aim to be clear and direct. When in doubt, keep your answer concise, Agnew notes.

“Keeping it short and sweet will communicate that you've made a decision, not that you've requested a negotiation.”.

Depending on where you left the conversation, you might have more steps to take.

It has been revealed that stick to your boundaries and promises. Did you offer to contribute money? Pay as agreed. Did you say no? Don’t let your friend's or family member’s persistence, or the opinions of other friends and relatives, change your mind.

Recent findings suggest that if you offered to provide nonfinancial support, Carlos recommends pointing your loved one to local government and nonprofit resources. That might include emergency rent assistance, cheap or free financial advice, food banks and career services.

It has been revealed that document the details and set the plan in motion. If you agreed to loan money, send your relative a quick text recapping the terms, Carlos indicates. He also suggests setting up a simple repayment system together, such as a recurring Zelle or Venmo transfer.

“Fewer reminders from you mean less tension,” he says.

Get outside help, if necessary. Despite your best efforts, it can be difficult to handle the situation on your own. If you’re feeling lingering stress or your family can’t reach a resolution, you might want to bring in some help, Agnew states.

She recommends working with a financial therapist or advisor, or using a financial wellness app.

That vehicle, likely branded as a Vactor or a Truvac, is just one small piece of the heavy-duty machinery keeping critical infrastructure functioning across North America. Federal Signal (FSS +5.81%) builds these essential machines, along with the sirens and lightbars that clear the way for emergency responders. The stock, which trades at $115.03 as of Nov. 23, 2026, has delivered a 6% return to shareholders over the past year.

In a recent development, federal Signal is the exact type of uber-niche industrial stock that I can't help but love. There isn't anything overly glamorous about the business (unless you're a big fan of street sweepers or vacuum trucks, at least); the stock simply outperforms over time. Over the last decade, FSS stock has generated annualized total returns of 22.3%, compared with the S&P 500's 13.9%.

In a recent development, leading the charge for Federal Signal's history of outperformance is its No. 1 market share across many niche vehicle platforms:.

It has been revealed that the manufacturer also believes it is the No. 3 or 4 player in refuse collection vehicles, the top dog in warning signals and industrial signaling equipment, and the No. 2 seller of public safety equipment (police car lights, for example).

Recent findings suggest that most importantly, it sells aftermarket parts for all of the vehicles and equipment mentioned. These aftermarket sales are a core part of Federal Signal's vision for the future and already account for 21% of total sales. They provide recurring, high-margin revenue that has helped the organization's net income margin double from 5.7% in 2016 to 11.7% today.

Best of all for investors, Federal Signal isn't an old-school, low-growth industrial firm. Successfully acquiring and integrating 18 businesses since 2016, FSS has grown sales at an 11.6% annualized clip over the last decade. With an impressive 15.5% return on invested capital, management seems to do a great job of targeting niche acquisitions that generate outsize returns over the long haul.

While I wouldn't call FSS stock cheap, trading at 23 times earnings and 19 times free cash flow (its "true" valuation is likely between those figures), its 14% sell-off since July makes for a reasonable entry point for interested investors. Generating 57% of its revenue from publicly funded end markets, and the rest from industrial, utility, oil and gas, and other critical industries that see Federal Signal's equipment as essentially non-discretionary, I think FSS stock is a great pick to continue beating the market over the next five years, and I will continue steadily adding to my shares.

    According to recent reports, recently news about big tech has often pulled rates down. Investor concerns about AI profitability keep cropping up, and when they do, tech stocks and bonds lose their appeal and Treasuries have been picking up the slack. Mortgage rates are generally benchmarked to the yield on the 10-year Treasury, and Treasury prices and yields move inversely. More demand for the 10YT drives prices up, and sends yields (and thus, mortgage rates) down.

    In a recent development, today's the opposite, though. Investors are having a bout of tech exuberance as Jensen Huang got reinstated as Nvidia CEO, and lots of excitement about tech stocks and bonds means less enthusiasm for Treasuries.

    Industry observers note that the Fed doesn't set mortgage rates, but its decisions influence the entire economy. That includes mortgage lenders, who tend to adjust rates ahead of its decisions. Raising the federal funds rate (the short-term borrowing rate the central bankers actually set) is the Fed's main tactic for managing inflation, so you can guess how things are likely to go at the Fed's December meeting. Markets already feel fairly certain about a quarter-percent rate hike.

    It has been revealed that we already know how PCE's likely to go, since it's the last of the three massive inflation measures to be released. We've already gotten last month's Consumer Price Index and Producer Price Index. October's CPI came in worse than predicted, showing widespread price increases. (When most of the increase is driven by one area, it's easier to be optimistic that inflation can be contained.) And October’s PPI revealed wholesale inflation climbed at its fastest pace in almost four years. PPI measures the price businesses pay for things, so it's often a preview of what consumers could face once those costs get passed along.

    Sources indicate that predictions for October PCE aren't great, so at this point the hope is that the numbers aren't even worse than expected. And again, PCE's out Wednesday morning.     10 stocks we like better than Bitcoin ›.

    According to recent reports, anthropic's (ANT -1.43%) much-anticipated blockbuster initial public offering (IPO) will go down as one of the highlights of the 2026 financial calendar after it raised a record $119.5 billion and surged 17% on its first day of trading. That stated, it subsequently erased most of those gains as tech stocks tumbled even further. Bitcoin (BTC -1.54%) fell to a two-year low of $55,150 on Nov. 21.

    CRYPTO · As of 7:01 AM ET 11/24/26.

    There's plenty to be noted about Anthropic's historic IPO, but while various crypto industry leaders were quick to pin the blame for Bitcoin's latest price plunge on the artificial intelligence (AI) giant, investor money moving to Anthropic is a small part of a much bigger picture.

    Industry observers note that as I write this (Nov. 23), Bitcoin has tumbled more than 25% in the past month. It's certainly true that the IPO soaked up some capital, but bigger factors are pressuring cryptocurrencies.

    Recent findings suggest that bear in mind that the S&P 500 and the Nasdaq Composite have fallen by 5.6% and 7.7%, respectively, in the past month and that Bitcoin's tumble started in October -- before both Nvidia's (NVDA +31.48%) woes and Anthropic's IPO. Investors are losing confidence across the board. Some concerns are unique to crypto, but this is not only a Bitcoin problem.

    Sources indicate that conerns about stricter regulation after the midterms, combined with higher Treasury yields and the strong possibility that the Federal Reserve will hike interest rates this year, all weigh heavily. Risk appetite wanes when investors can earn decent returns on safer assets. The $6.3 billion Binance hack at the end of October also undermined confidence in crypto, and leverage multiplied the fallout.

    Industry observers note that the AI sell-off shook Wall Street last week, making further volatility likely -- Bitcoin may fall even more. The bigger question is what might bring about a recovery and how this latest drop effects Bitcoin's long-term potential. For example, one strong argument for Bitcoin bulls is that it can act as a portfolio diversifier, and that still stands.

    Stubborn inflation, rising national debt, and ongoing geopolitical tensions all have the potential to weaken confidence in traditional currencies. As such, even though Bitcoin hasn't yet proven itself as a form of digital gold, it could still benefit from a flight to alternative assets. If a significant number of investors allocated just 1% or 2% of their portfolios to Bitcoin, that would drive considerable growth.

    Another is further mainstream blockchain adoption, including stablecoin usage, and growth in decentralized finance (DeFi). Bitcoin is the crypto leader, and as other cryptos grow, that helps Bitcoin. Bitcoin's Layer-2 solutions (blockchains that are built on top of the Bitcoin chain to improve performance) enhance its position as a secure settlement layer.

    Anthropic isn't to blame for Bitcoin's recent downturn, and it won't help it recover either. Instead, I'll be watching for regulatory moves that might galvanize the crypto industry, as well as any growth in stablecoin adoption. Institutional investment levels are a useful metric to track, too -- there's almost $81 billion in spot Bitcoin exchange-traded funds (ETFs) right now. If that starts to increase again, it is a sign that Bitcoin is regaining traction as a portfolio diversifier.

    I Rate Buy Now, Pay Later Apps; Here’s My Holiday Advice

    📅 23 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (984 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Nerdwallet

    ⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • As Americans compile their shopping lists ahead of the holiday season, I’ve been compiling my own kind of list — a list of 25 data points, gathered across six “buy now, pay later” (BNPL) apps, fed into a rubric of five categories and 22 subcategories, to produce a star rating for each app.
    • By the end, I know more about these apps than anyone should, and I’m eager to bestow my knowledge on the next unsuspecting person who utters “Klarna” in my vicinity.
    • I should have plenty of opportunities this year.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    As Americans compile their shopping lists ahead of the holiday season, I’ve been compiling my own kind of list — a list of 25 data points, gathered across six “buy now, pay later” (BNPL) apps, fed into a rubric of five categories and 22 subcategories, to produce a star rating for each app.

    It’s a major list. I check it twice (or 10 times).

    By the end, I know more about these apps than anyone should, and I’m eager to bestow my knowledge on the next unsuspecting person who utters “Klarna” in my vicinity.

    I should have plenty of opportunities this year. Nearly 2 in 5 holiday spenders (38%) plan to use BNPL, according to NerdWallet’s holiday spending report. Concerningly, the same report found that a higher share of BNPL owners expect they won’t be able to make their payments in full and on time compared to credit card users.

    Using BNPL for holiday shopping isn’t inherently bad, but there are risks, including sneaky fees and the ease of loan stacking across many providers.

    Here’s how to minimize those risks and set yourself up for success this holiday season.

    Brenton Harrison, a certified financial planner in Nashville, notes many of his clients are turning to buy now, pay later in the “messy middle of life,” when everyday expenses are high and budgets are tight. This is especially true during the holidays.

    “They have kids they're providing for, or they’re trying to go travel and see family,” Harrison states. “When those expenses pile up, it can be very attractive to be able to spread out payments.”.

    Since BNPL divides your total purchase into smaller installments, typically due every two weeks, it feels easier on your cash flow than having to pay all at once.

    It has been revealed that while Harrison is open to his clients using BNPL, he emphasizes how important it is to understand the terms before opting in. BNPL apps only require a soft credit pull and a short application. When you can apply for a loan in just a few clicks, it’s easy to miss when payments are due or whether they’ll include interest.

    But if clients understand the terms and are certain they can make the payments, Harrison indicates BNPL's set repayment schedule can be a better option than more open-ended financing.

    “With a credit card, [a holiday purchase] might be something that they buy over and over and over again, because that interest just continues to accrue over time, and they never pay it off,” he says.

    Recent findings suggest that not all BNPL apps are created equal. I measure the top apps across multiple categories, but I weigh affordability the highest. My thinking is if you’re already strapped for cash, it’s a bad idea to pay extra just to break up the payments.

    Sources indicate that there are providers, like Affirm and PayPal, that don’t charge interest with a common pay-in-four term (your total purchase, divided into four installments). They also charge no fees, including no late fees for missed payments.

    Compare that to apps, like Sezzle and Zip, that may charge an automatic service or origination fee with your first installment, as well as late fees.

    Recent findings suggest that long-term BNPL financing, which can stretch months or even years, usually includes interest, expressed as an annual percentage rate or APR. This is a more expensive payment option than a zero-interest pay-in-four.

    In a recent development, pay close attention to your checkout screen to see what you’re offered. Are the installment amounts equal or is the first installment higher than the others? That may mean there’s a fee. Do you see an APR listed? That means you’re paying interest.

    Harrison points out that just because a store partners with a BNPL manufacturer doesn’t mean that’s your only option. Download a different BNPL app, search for the store and see if you get access to better terms, like a 0% offer.

    Taking out multiple loans with different BNPL providers is known as “loan stacking,” and it’s risky.

    Because you’re juggling different payment amounts due on different days, it’s hard to keep track of what’s coming out of your bank account. This is especially true if you set up automatic payments, which most BNPL apps require. If you overdraw your checking account, your bank will likely charge a fee.

    It has been revealed that according to research published in August by the Federal Reserve, 11% percent of BNPL users had a BNPL payment trigger an overdraft or nonsufficient funds fee from their bank in the prior year. People with less savings were even more likely to pay fees.

    Before applying for multiple BNPL loans, look at a typical month of expenses and ask if there’s extra room in your budget for those payments, Harrison claims.

    “If you’re just assuming that because you’re spreading it out that you’ll be able to pay it, that's where I think people can get in trouble,” he says. “They set it and forget it, and they don't realize, ‘Oh, I am in no better position to pay that next month than I am this month, or I have three of these going at the same time, and collectively, it's more than I can manage.’”.

    Most apps send payment reminders, so you can potentially reschedule the payment or change your payment method.

    Industry observers note that still, it’s best to avoid the headache to begin with. If you’re feeling pressured to spend more this holiday season, communicate your limits clearly with loved ones, Harrison says, and avoid any loans you can’t comfortably repay.

    In a recent development, “Think about the purchase itself, especially around the holidays,” he states. “There's a major difference between something that I can pay off over three months and something that I should have never been buying in the first place.”.

    Addas a preferred source on Google.

    Tech Report: Cybersecurity Practices That Can Create A False Sense Of Security

    📅 23 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 7 min read (1337 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Forbes

    ⏱️ ~7 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Industry observers note that organizations invest significant time and resources in cybersecurity measures designed to protect their systems, data and operations.
    • According to recent reports, for tech leaders, the challenge is recognizing when established security practices are effectively reducing risk and when they may be simply creating the appearance of preparedness.
    • It has been revealed that “We have 24/7 monitoring” is not the same as, “We will catch an problem at 2 a.m.” This is truly a false sense of security unless your teams have fine-tuned alerts very well over time for your situations and context.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Industry observers note that organizations invest significant time and resources in cybersecurity measures designed to protect their systems, data and operations. However, even practices that seem responsible can create a false sense of security—especially when they’re treated as substitutes for more comprehensive protection and ongoing risk assessment.

    According to recent reports, for tech leaders, the challenge is recognizing when established security practices are effectively reducing risk and when they may be simply creating the appearance of preparedness. Here, Forbes Technology Council members highlight common cybersecurity practices and beliefs that can give organizations misplaced confidence and explain what to do instead.

    It has been revealed that “We have 24/7 monitoring” is not the same as, “We will catch an problem at 2 a.m.” This is truly a false sense of security unless your teams have fine-tuned alerts very well over time for your situations and context. That means TP/FP are identified, and actual signals are not lost in the high-volume alert noise. To test, inject a true alert at an inconvenient hour and see if ops is detecting it and acting upon it. Monitoring is mostly a comfort unless you make it a security control. - Pradeep Sandhu, Cywarden, Inc.

    Recent findings suggest that the fundamental assumption behind traditional cybersecurity is that all the technology in your security stack will behave exactly as designed, requiring little oversight. This could not be further from the truth. Constant governance and visibility into your security system is no longer an option. It is a necessity that can’t be overlooked or underestimated, and it’s a critical issue that must be addressed, especially as we navigate the uncharted territory of AI. - Kevin Lynch, Optiv.

    Recent findings suggest that forbes Technology Council is an invitation-only community for world-class CIOs, CTOs and technology executives. Do I qualify?

    According to recent reports, prioritizing security by a generic risk model describes the average organization, which does not exist. One bank had 362 vulnerabilities under attack in its network that global data never saw. A score trained on everyone is a statement about no one. - Michael Roytman, Empirical Security.

    Recent findings suggest that as a CISO, I’ve sat through HiTrust, SOC 2 and PCI audits, and I value them. But a clean report is a snapshot of scoped controls and evidence chosen for an auditor to see, not proof we’d stop a real attacker. The danger is when “we passed” becomes the finish line and the board sees a green light. I treat audits as the floor, then measure what matters: real prevention, detection and remediation speed. - Lane Sullivan, Concentric AI.

    It has been revealed that many organizations mistake end-to-end encryption for security. Encryption answers one question: Can someone read the message in transit? It notes nothing about who is on the other end or whether a record survives. Further, the same encryption that keeps attackers out can end up keeping the firm out, too. Security means governing the conversation at the source, with verified identities, managed access and a record the firm owns and can act on. - Dima Gutzeit, LeapXpert.

    Sources indicate that treating an approved business application as permanently trusted can create unchecked risk. Vendors now add AI agents and automation to software enterprises already use, giving new capabilities access to existing data, permissions and workflows. Security teams need to reassess what those applications can do as features change, not rely on the risk profile established when they were procured. - Ofer Klein, Reco.

    Software from an approved vendor, known repository, signed package or internal developer can still contain malicious or unintended behavior. Source and provenance are vital, but they do not show what the finished code will actually do. Organizations should verify behavior before execution, not inherit trust from where the code came from. - Ken Ammon, CodeHunter.

    Recent findings suggest that early in my career, the problem was, “We don’t know what we have.” Today, most teams have dashboards full of alerts and findings, but visibility doesn’t equal security. If the data from your environment is not contextualized into actionable, cross-domain insights and proactive remediation workflows, you’ve just documented your exposure in more detail rather than successfully mitigating it. - Sivan Tehila, Onyxia Cyber.

    Sources indicate that A common misconception is that if an email passes through a security gateway, it must be safe. While traditional gateways catch known threats, they’re less effective against AI-driven attacks that don’t rely on malicious links or attachments. These newer attacks look and sound legitimate, making them harder to spot. That’s why organizations must pay attention to communication patterns. - Eyal Benishti, IRONSCALES.

    Sources indicate that A green dashboard does not truly mean your business is secure. No alerts may signal gaps in visibility, not an absence of threats. Organizations need security that connects signals across their environment, backed by experts who monitor, investigate and respond 24/7. Regularly test your defenses to confirm teams can detect suspicious activity and act promptly to contain threats before they do harm. - Neal Bradbury, Barracuda.

    Sources indicate that one of the biggest misconceptions about open-source security is that finding vulnerabilities means you’re securing your software. Scanners and AI agents can flag thousands of risks, but without a clear remediation path, they create backlogs instead of protection. For end-of-life open-source software, the stakes are even higher. When official patches stop, vulnerabilities don’t. - Aaron Mitchell, HeroDevs.

    A dangerous belief is that more security tools automatically mean better security. In reality, too many disconnected tools can create blind spots, duplicate alerts and unclear ownership. A mature security posture is not defined by how much technology has been purchased but by how quickly the organization can detect, understand and contain a real threat. - Dr. Chiranjiv Roy, C5i.ai.

    Vendor security questionnaires feel thorough, but they capture a one-time self-assessment from direct suppliers and say little about the vendors behind them. Risk changes constantly and often sits several tiers deep, so treat these questionnaires as a starting point, then pair them with continuous monitoring of the extended sub-tier supplier network for proactive supplier risk mitigation. - Yardley Pohl, interos.ai.

    Sources indicate that poorly executed phishing tests can do far more to damage employee trust than they will ever benefit an organization’s cybersecurity capability. Activities that penalize individuals, don’t result in meaningful and engaged education, or become so frequent that they annoy and create resentment do little to strengthen your cyber defenses. - Kim Bozzella, Protiviti.

    In a recent development, I think relying too heavily on periodic security audits can create a false sense of confidence. They’re valuable, but technology changes rapidly, especially as teams introduce new tools and AI into their workflows. I’ve learned that it’s key to keep reviewing how systems are actually being used, who has access and where new risks may be developing between audits. - Deniz Gezgin, Eightpoint.

    Industry observers note that mandatory password rotation is often mistaken for effective cybersecurity. Requiring employees to change passwords every 60 to 90 days can encourage predictable variations and credential reuse, potentially increasing security risks. Organizations should prioritize phishing-resistant multifactor authentication, compromised-credential detection and risk-based access controls over routine password expiration. - Gouri Sankar Dash, Tata Consultancy Services.

    Recent findings suggest that treating successful backups as proof of recovery can create false confidence. A backup job can finish successfully while a full restoration still fails or takes too long. Test recovery of a complete business workflow in an isolated environment, including its dependencies, and measure the time until people can actually use it. - Shahen Minasyan, Twin Peaks Inc. (TPI).

    It has been revealed that access and authentication controls are paramount to any internal system, but with AI agents now working alongside humans, impersonation is becoming a growing threat. These tools often rely on being able to access the same files and systems you can access. It may be productive, but left unattended, it’s risky. Building in systemic limitations to what AI agents can do on your behalf is an important consideration. - Matt Wielbut, Openly.

    Investors with a long-term horizon can look beyond the ongoing volatility and track the recommendations of top Wall Street analysts to pick attractive stocks with strong long-term growth potential.

    Here are three stocks favored by some of Wall Street's top pros, according to TipRanks, a platform that ranks analysts based on their past performance.

    Health insurer UnitedHealth delivered better-than-expected results for the third quarter of 2026. The company also raised its full-year earnings outlook, reflecting continued progress on its turnaround initiative.

    It has been revealed that following the Q3 print, Morgan Stanley analyst Erin Wright reiterated a buy rating on UNH stock with a price target of $529. "UNH's beat & raise reinforces turnaround momentum, with improving MA [Medicare Advantage]/Optum Health supporting a higher '26 EPS baseline & upside to '27 consensus," noted Wright.

    In a recent development, the five-star analyst added that better-than-expected performance in the UnitedHealthcare and Optum Health businesses supported another upgrade to the manufacturer's 2026 adjusted earnings per share outlook to at least $20.50. Wright noted that UNH raised the earnings guidance despite incremental investments planned for the fourth quarter of 2026.

    Sources indicate that furthermore, Wright highlighted management's view that the consensus 2027 EPS of $22.63 was too conservative. Reaching even the low end of the company's 13% to 16% long-term EPS growth target would imply an EPS of $23.17.

    It has been revealed that wright raised her 2026 EPS estimate to $20.65 from $19.82 and 2027 EPS to $23.24 from $22.54, reflecting the latest upside and an improving 2026 medical loss ratio to 87.4% from 88.1%. Overall, she believes that UNH's operational performance continues to improve, increasing her confidence in its UHC strategy and Optum Health turnaround execution.

    Wright ranks No. 264 among more than 12,500 analysts tracked by TipRanks. Her ratings have been successful 64% of the time, delivering an average return of 15%. See UnitedHealth Ownership Structure on TipRanks.

    In a recent development, social media giant Meta Platforms has been making headlines since the launch of its Muse AI agent, which is seeing solid traction. Investors look forward to updates on the firm's AI strategy when it announces its third-quarter results on Oct. 21.

    Heading into Q3 earnings, Guggenheim analyst Michael Morris maintained a buy rating on Meta stock and increased his price target to $850 from $700, reflecting higher estimates for 2027. He expects Muse usage momentum and engagement levels to shape investor sentiment into the Q3 earnings call.

    Specifically, Morris highlighted that, according to Apptopia, Muse reached 1.3 million daily active users in five weeks versus 300,000 in the first week. Given that Muse's current adoption represents less than 0.05% of Meta's 3.6 billion daily active user base, the analyst expects management to prioritize boosting usage over near-term monetization.

    "Over time, we believe Muse monetizes primarily through businesses paying to reach consumers through their agents, consistent with the economics of Meta's core advertising business, rather than consumer wallets," said the five-star analyst. He added that the checkout integrations with Shopify and PayPal reflect this framework.

    While there are concerns that a rival could overtake Muse or the recently launched Muse Wonder and push Meta into a prolonged cycle of overinvestment, Morris remains bullish due to the company's strong record in scaling WhatsApp and competing strongly with TikTok via Reels as well as free distribution to an extensive user base.

    Recent findings suggest that morris ranks No. 629 among more than 12,500 analysts tracked by TipRanks. His ratings have been successful 57% of the time, delivering an average return of 13.2%. See Meta Platforms KPIs on TipRanks.

    Next is semiconductor company Marvell Technology. Earlier this month, Marvell held its Investor Day, where it raised its total addressable market estimate to $400 billion by 2030, reflecting solid AI-led demand tailwinds.

    After hosting a non-deal roadshow with Marvell's senior management following the Investor Day, Stifel analyst Tore Svanberg reiterated a buy rating on the stock with a price target of $370.

    The five-star analyst stated that a major focus of the roadshow was the XPU and XPU Attach mix, as Marvell's Custom business expands toward its FY31 revenue target of $30 billion. In this regard, management reiterated that it expects a balanced mix of XPU and XPU Attach revenue in FY31, though it noted that either segment could grow rapidly enough to shift the mix toward 60/40 or 40/60.

    It has been revealed that while XPU drove most of the nearly $1.5 billion Custom revenue in FY26, Svanberg expects Marvell's XPU Attach business to grow substantially through the end of the decade, leading to a more balanced mix in this business. At the Investor Day event, the firm raised its FY29 Custom target from more than $10 billion to over $12 billion, mainly driven by strength in the XPU Attach business.

    Sources indicate that svanberg mentioned that another key topic in the roadshow was whether Marvell can secure enough capacity to meet its raised targets. Management said that it met with suppliers ahead of Investor Day to share its five-year goals and received commitments to support these targets. The analyst believes that Marvell's supply chain commitments give it a competitive edge over rivals as customers seek reliable partners for large-scale infrastructure buildouts.

    Svanberg ranks No. 91 among more than 12,500 analysts tracked by TipRanks. His ratings have been profitable 58% of the time, delivering an average return of 31.8%. See Marvell Technology Statistics on TipRanks.

    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    By Sean Williams – Nov 24, 2026 at 4:06AM EST.

    10 stocks we like better than McDonald's ›.

    Some of the world's most successful money managers oversee hundreds of trades per quarter -- but that doesn't hold a candle to the jaw-dropping activity in President Donald Trump's investment account. The president's independent, third-party investment team has executed in the neighborhood of 30,000 trades since January 2025, according to reports filed with the U.S. Office of Government Ethics (OGE).

    According to recent reports, according to the latest OGE filing, Trump's investment team executed 751 trades in September. This included dumping up to $5,000,000 in McDonald's (MCD +1.15%) stock and piling up to $25,000,000 into the Vanguard Dividend Appreciation ETF (VIG +2.18%).

    President Trump's independent, third-party investment team oversaw 751 trades in September. Image source: Official White House Photo by Daniel Torok.

    Although Donald Trump is a connoisseur of McDonald's food, his third-party investment team isn't. Though several small trades were executed in McDonald's stock during September, the $1,000,001-$5,000,000 sale on the 23rd ties for the largest disposition of the month.

    Despite shares being historically inexpensive, the organization is navigating numerous headwinds that aren't easy fixes.

    NYSE · As of 4:00 PM ET 11/23/26.

    Recent findings suggest that for example, McDonald's is being hit on both ends due to inflation (rising prices). On the one hand, the manufacturer's value menu risks pressuring its margins amid persistently elevated inflation. Conversely, raising prices to protect its margins could be off-putting to the low- and middle-income customers that have long been the lifeblood of the company's customer base.

    Furthermore, while McDonald's NEXT strategy offers promise of a turnaround, the tech giant's plans to spend up to $8.5 billion through 2036 to assist its franchisees provide minimal near-term benefits. In a stock market that's been dominated by growth stocks, the last thing investors want to hear is that it could take years before the company's investments really start to pay off.

    At the other end of the spectrum, the president's independent, third-party investment team scooped up between $5,000,001 and $25,000,000 of the Vanguard Dividend Appreciation ETF on Sept. 23.

    Vanguard's dividend-focused ETF closed October with nearly $136 billion in assets under management and a portfolio containing a blend of 333 value and growth stocks. The common theme is that these are large-cap companies that have increased their annual payouts for at least 10 consecutive years. In other words, these are time-tested businesses with rich histories of profitability and transparent growth outlooks.

    Additionally, the Vanguard Dividend Appreciation ETF removes companies in the top 25% of yield to avoid potential yield traps. While this exchange-traded fund's 1.5% yield isn't jaw-dropping, its payout is incredibly safe.

    3 of the most popular dividend ETFs, and how each one picks its stocks 👇$VIG: 10+ years of dividend raises, skipping the top 25% highest yielders$DGRO: 5+ years of raises and a payout ratio under 75%$SCHD: 10+ years of dividends, then the top 100 by yield, growth and… pic.twitter.com/u8UN6WqRwM.

    In a recent development, since this is a passive ETF with minimal turnover, it has a minuscule net expense ratio of 0.04%. Only $0.40 of every $1,000 invested goes toward management/marketing fees, enabling investors to retain more of their principal and long-term gains.

    It has been revealed that best of all, dividend stocks have an extensive history of outperforming publicly traded companies that don't offer a regular dividend. In "The Power of Dividends: Past, Present, and Future," the analysts at Hartford Funds, in collaboration with Ned Davis Research, found that dividend growers and initiators averaged a 10.22% annual return from 1973 to 2025. By comparison, the non-payers trudged their way to an average annual return of 4.21% over the same time frame.

    Dividend stocks are a smart way to hedge in a historically pricey stock market.

    • Sources indicate that running out of money is something even wealthy retirees worry about.
    • Boosting your Social Security checks may not entirely alleviate that fear.
    • Recent findings suggest that you're allowed to claim retirement benefits from Social Security at any point once you turn 62.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    By Maurie Backman – Nov 24, 2026 at 4:18AM EST.

    Sources indicate that running out of money is something even wealthy retirees worry about. After all, you have no idea going into retirement how long you'll live, what your exact expenses will look like, and what financial surprises might be in store. So even if you manage to accumulate a few million dollars in a retirement account, there may be a nagging fear that it'll all be gone one day.

    Boosting your Social Security checks may not entirely alleviate that fear. But it could help. And you should know that there's an easy way to score a massive boost to your monthly benefits.

    Recent findings suggest that you're allowed to claim retirement benefits from Social Security at any point once you turn 62. And you can collect those monthly checks without a reduction once you reach full retirement age, which is 67 if you were born in 1960 or later.

    Recent findings suggest that but for each year you delay your Social Security claim past full retirement age, until age 70, your benefits get a permanent 8% boost. So if your full retirement age is 67, you have an opportunity to set yourself up with monthly checks that are 24% larger. And that could give you the peace of mind you need to feel more comfortable navigating retirement.

    It has been revealed that the more money Social Security pays you each month, the less you should need to tap your savings. And the less you withdraw from your savings each month, the lower your chances should be of running out.

    Industry observers note that being able to rely more on Social Security could be especially helpful during periods of market decline. Riding out downturns and letting your savings recover each time should reduce your chances of reaching $0.

    Plus, Social Security benefits get built-in inflation protection. Each year, they're eligible for a cost-of-living adjustment, or COLA. The larger your benefits are to begin with, the more valuable those COLAs should be over time, and the more you can safeguard your finances during periods when costs are on the rise.

    Recent findings suggest that delaying Social Security isn't necessarily the best choice for everyone. There may be good reasons to claim benefits sooner, such as poor health, a pressing financial need due to a layoff, a major expense that can't wait, or other circumstances.

    It has been revealed that but if running out of money in retirement is a big fear of yours, it pays to consider delaying your Social Security claim as long as possible. Boosted benefits could help you feel better about your financial situation, which could lead you to enjoy retirement more overall.

    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    According to recent reports, etihad Guest, the loyalty program of Abu Dhabi-based Etihad Airways, is expanding its U.S. presence by introducing two new credit cards. Most people won’t get much value from these cards, but they can make sense for Etihad frequent flyers who want elite status.

    Recent findings suggest that the two cards are the Etihad Guest Visa Signature® Card ($99 annual fee) and the Etihad Guest Premier Visa Signature® Card ($499 annual fee). Issued by the First National Bank of Omaha, both offer faster pathways to earning and maintaining elite status and the ability to earn extra miles on Etihad purchases.

    Industry observers note that they also offer extra miles on international transactions (neither has foreign transaction fees) and purchases with Etihad’s partner airlines, which include U.S. carriers like American Airlines and JetBlue Airways.

    Here’s what you need to know about the cards.

    The Etihad Guest Visa Signature® Card comes with a $99 annual fee, and it earns Etihad Guest miles at the following rates:.

    3 miles per $1 spent on Etihad purchases.

    2 miles per $1 spent on Etihad partner airline purchases.

    It has been revealed that 2 miles per $1 spent on non-U.S. purchases.

    In a recent development, 1 mile per $1 spent on all other U.S. purchases.

    Welcome offer: Through Feb. 3, 2027, the card is offering the following welcome offer for fresh applicants: Earn up to 40,000 welcome Etihad Guest Miles, including 10,000 miles after the first purchase and an additional 30,000 miles after spending $3,000 within the first three billing cycles after account opening.

    Elite status benefits: You’ll also get Etihad Silver status after your first Etihad purchase within 90 days of opening your account. Unlike most airlines, that entry-level status is enough to get you into the business class lounge when traveling through Etihad’s hub at Abu Dhabi’s Zayed International Airport.

    You can retain that status by spending $20,000 a year on the card, or $3,000 a year on Etihad purchases.

    The Etihad Guest Premier Visa Signature® Card comes with a $499 annual fee, and it earns Etihad Guest miles at the following rates:.

    5 miles per $1 spent on Etihad purchases.

    3 miles per $1 spent on Etihad partner airline purchases.

    2 miles per $1 spent on non-U.S. purchases.

    It has been revealed that 1 mile per $1 spent on all other U.S. purchases.

    The only differences in rewards between the premium and standard cards are increased earning rates for eligible airline purchases.

    Industry observers note that welcome offer: Through Feb. 3, 2027, the premium card offers a higher welcome offer compared to the standard card: Earn up to 60,000 welcome Etihad Guest Miles, including 20,000 miles after the first purchase and 40,000 miles after spending $7,000 within the first three billing cycles after account opening.

    Elite status benefits: The premium card offers a faster track to elite status: automatic Silver status upon card approval and Gold status after your first Etihad purchase within 90 days of opening your account.

    Recent findings suggest that to maintain Gold status, you’ll need to spend $40,000 a year on the card, or $8,000 on Etihad purchases. Otherwise, you’ll have Silver status.

    Wi-Fi benefit: After your first Etihad purchase, you’ll get 3,000 Etihad Guest miles, enough to cover Wi-Fi costs on a long-haul Etihad flight. You’ll then get those miles again after each cardholder anniversary.

    Industry observers note that travel benefits: The card offers a statement credit for Global Entry or TSA PreCheck and select travel protections. If you already have a premium travel card, you might already have access to these perks.

    The card also includes a Priority Pass lounge access membership. However, an Etihad spokesperson told NerdWallet that it’s the entry-level membership tier, so you’ll need to pay for yourself and guests each time you visit a Priority Pass lounge. Most premium credit cards in the U.S. that offer Priority Pass allow complimentary visits for at least the cardholder.

    The Etihad cards make the most sense for Etihad’s frequent flyers who are flying to or connecting through Abu Dhabi several times a year.

    That’s because the standard card’s accelerated pathway to Etihad Guest’s Silver status tier can unlock the ability to choose business class lounge access in Abu Dhabi as a status perk.

    With the premium card, you get a fast track to Gold. If you select lounge access as a Gold status perk, you can not only bring a guest on the same flight into the lounge, but also access Etihad’s worldwide lounge network. That includes Etihad’s own lounges in Newly introduced York and Washington, D.C., as well as most partner lounges at other Etihad destinations.

    Industry observers note that bear in mind that while Etihad has many partnerships with other airlines, it’s not part of an alliance, so you don’t get lounge benefits when traveling on partners. You’ll need to be flying on an Etihad-operated flight to get into the lounge.

    If you primarily fly with other carriers, then Etihad status will have limited upside for you.

    However, the Priority Pass lounge membership that comes with the premium card does not have that restriction. You can access Priority Pass lounges while flying on any airline, although you’ll need to pay an additional per-person $35 fee each visit.

    According to recent reports, the earning rates on the Etihad cards are lackluster for everyday spenders. The bonus categories are for airline purchases with Etihad and its partners, as well as international spending.

    That means your day-to-day purchases at home, like groceries, dining out and gas, earn only 1 mile per $1 spent.

    Plus, there are more ways to earn Etihad Guest miles than spending on an Etihad credit card. For example, you can transfer points to Etihad Guest from Bilt Rewards, Capital One and Citi ThankYou.

    In a recent development, those programs offer cards that typically have better benefits and bonus categories, and they offer flexibility on how you can use your points and miles. With an Etihad card, you can only earn Etihad Guest miles, which expire after 18 months without qualifying flight activity. (If you’re not traveling on Etihad or its partners at least once every 18 months, then you definitely should not get the cards.).

    One of the most interesting perks of the upcoming cards is the bonus category for spending with Etihad partner airlines — 2 miles per $1 for the standard card and 3 miles per $1 for the premium version. Typically, airline credit cards reward customers only for spending on the airline, not partners.

    There are better cards available, though. Some offer as many or even more points per $1 on flights purchased directly from airlines.

    If you want the card solely to earn more Etihad Guest miles, then the answer for most people is no.

    While you can earn more miles for purchases with Etihad and partner airlines, the earning rates aren’t attractive enough to justify the annual fees, especially when compared with existing cards with currencies that transfer to Etihad Guest.

    Status chasers could benefit from the fast track to elite status — but you would need to be a fairly frequent Etihad flyer to really take advantage of your elite benefits.

    Tech Report: What Is a Reconditioning Fee on a Used Car?

    📅 24 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (728 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Nerdwallet

    ⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Industry observers note that A reconditioning fee is an added dealer charge you might find when buying a used car.
    • The reconditioning process varies between dealerships, but typically includes these steps:.
    • Sources indicate that A visual exterior inspection.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Industry observers note that A reconditioning fee is an added dealer charge you might find when buying a used car. It’s intended to cover any costs the dealer incurs to make sure a used car is showroom-ready, from mechanical inspections to detailing.

    The reconditioning process varies between dealerships, but typically includes these steps:.

    Sources indicate that A visual exterior inspection. An auto tech does a quick walk-around the vehicle and notes any corrosion, damage or wear.

    Sources indicate that an interior inspection. The engine and auto interior are examined and tested, and any problems are documented.

    A test drive. The car is taken out for a drive to check that it runs well and that the radio, brakes, A/C and other components are all functioning properly.

    It has been revealed that service and repair. Any interior or exterior mechanical, functional or cosmetic issues that were found are repaired, including paint, dents, oil changes and major engine work.

    Inspection. Once repairs are completed, the car is inspected again to make sure everything looks and functions as it should.

    Sources indicate that detailing. This includes deep interior, engine and exterior cleaning as well as any necessary leather refurbishing, bumper repair or wheel restoration.

    Reconditioning fees are legal, but that doesn’t mean you have to pay them. Dealers can charge whatever they want for a reconditioning fee, and it’s not uncommon to find them ranging from around $500 to over $2,000.

    In a recent development, the good news: Reconditioning fees, like most dealer extras, can be negotiable. Ask the dealer for a breakdown of the reconditioning fee to see what kind of work was done to prepare the car for sale. If the work was minor but the fee is high — for example, if they’re asking for $1,995 but replaced the floor mats only — that’s a good sign it’s a bogus charge.

    It has been revealed that however, when it comes time for negotiation, don’t just haggle over the reconditioning fee or other individual fees. The best way to negotiate is to focus on the out-the-door price, or the total amount you’re paying for the car. This simplifies the negotiation process and keeps you focused on the true price of your car.

    All dealers invest some amount in reconditioning, but those costs are often built into the dealer’s asking price for a vehicle, rather than as a separate charge.

    Sources indicate that some dealers opt to add a reconditioning fee to the bill because it allows them to advertise a lower asking price online, which doesn’t include fees. It’s a tactic to get you into their dealership, since the asking price is lower than that of other dealerships.

    However, once you arrive, you may find that the out-the-door price is the same — or more — compared with what other dealers are asking.

    According to recent reports, some car-buying experts recommend avoiding dealerships that charge reconditioning fees altogether. But remember that the out-the-door price is what matters at the end of the day, so it’s worth comparing prices at multiple dealerships to find the best deal.

    Sources indicate that reddit is an online forum where users share their thoughts in “threads” on various topics. The popular site includes plenty of discussion on financial subjects like car buying, so we sifted through Reddit threads to get a sense of how users feel about reconditioning fees. People post anonymously, so we cannot confirm their individual experiences or circumstances.

    Sources indicate that reddit people are generally skeptical toward reconditioning fees. Many users view these fees as a bait-and-switch tactic: dealers advertise an attractive price online and then tack on the fee at the dealership, inflating the actual out-the-door cost well above what was listed. Car buyers frequently share stories of being hit with reconditioning fees ranging from a few hundred dollars up to $2,000 or more, often with little or no evidence of what work was actually done.

    It has been revealed that car-buying experts on Reddit point out that most dealerships already build reconditioning costs into the sticker price, so if the fee is listed separately, the dealership may be double-dipping. Several consumers suggest that car buyers ask their dealer for an itemized breakdown of the work done, but most users recommend negotiating the total out-the-door price rather than individual fees.

    CVS Has Beaten Earnings Estimates 6 Quarters Straight. Why Is the Stock Under $90?

    📅 24 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (860 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Fool

    ⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • In a recent development, CVS Health (CVS -1.47%) has consistently beaten Wall Street's earnings expectations, raised its financial guidance, and improved profitability across its major businesses.
    • The tech giant's latest results included $108.4 billion in revenue, up 5.4% year over year, and adjusted earnings of $2.09 per share, compared with $1.60 a year earlier.
    • So why isn't Wall Street rewarding CVS for its improving financial performance?
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    By Jeff Siegel – Nov 24, 2026 at 4:30AM EST.

    In a recent development, CVS Health (CVS -1.47%) has consistently beaten Wall Street's earnings expectations, raised its financial guidance, and improved profitability across its major businesses. Yet its stock continues trading below $90. In fact, CVS closed at $81.35 on Nov. 18, down 5.2% for the day, despite reporting another strong quarter earlier this month.

    The tech giant's latest results included $108.4 billion in revenue, up 5.4% year over year, and adjusted earnings of $2.09 per share, compared with $1.60 a year earlier. Analysts had expected roughly $1.65 per share. Management also raised its full-year adjusted earnings forecast to at least $8.20 per share, up from its previous range of $7.90 to $8.10.

    So why isn't Wall Street rewarding CVS for its improving financial performance?

    Sources indicate that CVS has spent the past several years managing rising healthcare costs, particularly in its Aetna insurance business. When patients require more medical care than insurers anticipated, insurance companies must pay more in claims. Unless premiums rise enough to offset those expenses, profitability suffers. CVS experienced precisely that problem.

    Recent findings suggest that in 2024 and part of 2025, its insurance business struggled with elevated medical costs, particularly among Medicare Advantage members. Those pressures contributed to disappointing financial results and forced management to reconsider pricing, benefits, and membership growth. Fortunately, the latest numbers show improvement.

    NYSE · As of 4:00 PM ET 11/23/26.

    According to recent reports, in Q3, Aetna's medical benefit ratio fell to 91.3%, compared with 92.8% a year earlier. That ratio measures how much of an insurer's premium revenue goes toward paying medical claims. A lower number generally means the company retains more money to cover administrative expenses and generate profits. Still, a 91.3% medical benefit ratio leaves relatively little room for unexpected increases in healthcare costs.

    On Nov. 4, CVS announced looks to separate into two publicly traded companies. One will include Aetna, CVS Caremark, CVS Specialty, Oak Street Health, and Signify Health. The other will operate approximately 9,000 CVS pharmacies, as well as MinuteClinic and related businesses. Management expects to complete the separation during the first half of 2028.

    It has been revealed that the announcement surprised investors. As a result, CVS shares plunged 12.5% that day, despite the company's earnings beat and improved guidance.

    The decision also marks a departure from the strategy CVS pursued when it acquired Aetna for approximately $70 billion in 2018. At the time, management argued that combining insurance, pharmacies, and healthcare services would create a more efficient healthcare company. Now, CVS believes separating its retail pharmacy operations from its insurance and healthcare services businesses will provide greater flexibility and allow each company to focus on its own priorities.

    CVS also faces pressure in its pharmacy and pharmacy benefit management businesses. Pharmacy benefit managers (PBMs) negotiate drug prices and manage prescription benefits for insurers and employers.

    CVS Caremark is one of the country's largest PBMs, but the industry faces increasing regulatory scrutiny over drug pricing, rebates, and transparency. Changes to reimbursement arrangements could reduce profitability.

    Meanwhile, CVS's retail pharmacy business continues to deal with reimbursement pressure and competition. Third-quarter retail pharmacy revenue declined 2% to approximately $35.5 billion, although adjusted operating income increased 10.6% to $1.64 billion. Prescription volume also increased. Those results suggest the business remains financially healthy, but revenue growth isn't guaranteed.

    It has been revealed that at $81.35 per share, CVS trades for approximately 9.9 times management's projected 2026 adjusted earnings of at least $8.20 per share. That's a relatively modest valuation for a company expected to generate more than $420 billion in annual revenue.

    Sources indicate that CVS also generated $15.3 billion in operating cash flow during the first nine months of 2026, and management recently increased its full-year operating cash flow guidance to at least $15.5 billion, up from its previous forecast of at least $11.5 billion. The company also expects adjusted earnings of at least $8.65 per share in 2027.

    At $81.35, the forward price-to-earnings ratio is approximately 9.4. However, adjusted earnings exclude certain expenses, and strong operating cash flow doesn't automatically translate into free cash flow available to shareholders. CVS still needs to fund capital expenditures, service its debt, and finance the planned separation.

    In a recent development, CVS's valuation suggests investors have already priced in considerable uncertainty. The insurance business is recovering, pharmacy profitability is improving, and management continues raising earnings expectations. But the proposed breakup complicates the outlook, while rising medical costs and regulatory changes remain legitimate concerns.

    According to recent reports, I'd be reluctant to dismiss CVS simply because its stock has struggled, though. If management delivers on its 2027 earnings guidance and successfully separates the businesses, today's valuation could prove attractive.
