    General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Nerdwallet ↗ Open Full Page

    Industry News: What Are Repositioning Cruises?

    📅 24 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (1047 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Nerdwallet

    ⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • A repositioning cruise is a one-way sailing that moves a ship from one region to another.
    • Repositioning cruises are most common in spring (roughly March to May) and fall (roughly September to November), though they can occur at other times of year.
    • Recent findings suggest that because ships are crossing oceans, these trips often include many days at sea.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    A repositioning cruise is a one-way sailing that moves a ship from one region to another. For example, many ships sail in the Mediterranean Sea during the summer and move to the Caribbean Sea for the winter, and that trip between the two is a repositioning cruise.

    Repositioning cruises are most common in spring (roughly March to May) and fall (roughly September to November), though they can occur at other times of year.

    Recent findings suggest that because ships are crossing oceans, these trips often include many days at sea. For some travelers, that’s a chance to relax and enjoy the ship’s onboard amenities. Sometimes, these sailings can also be cheaper than traditional cruises.

    One key consideration for a repositioning cruise is that the embarkation and disembarkation ports will be different. This means you generally can’t buy a standard round-trip flight to and from the same city. Instead, you’ll need transportation to where the cruise starts and another way home from where it ends, which usually means two one-way flights (or one open-jaw ticket) unless you live near one of the ports. While these one-way sailings may be more affordable than traditional cruises, airfare costs may be higher.

    This could be a great opportunity to redeem miles for your flight.

    Another feature that sets these cruises apart is that stops along the way tend to include ports that aren’t traditionally part of regular itineraries. These might include islands like Bermuda, the Azores or the Canary Islands, and on some northern routes, Greenland.

    According to recent reports, just keep in mind that the main purpose of these sailings is to get to a upcoming region for the next season’s itineraries rather than make daily port stops. So if you’re someone who wants to visit as many places as possible on a cruise, a repositioning sailing may not be the ideal choice.

    In a recent development, repositioning cruises are often longer than standard cruises, commonly running two to three weeks compared with about a week for a typical sailing, which may appeal to travelers looking for an extended vacation. The experience is often more relaxed, with many days at sea and less of a rush to book shore excursions or visit crucial sites when off the ship.

    Recent findings suggest that if there are particular ships with certain amenities — like tattoo parlors or massive waterparks — that you really want to experience, keep in mind that not all ships reposition between regions. Some stay in certain regions year-round.

    For ships that do change locations for the season, there are plenty of onboard activities to fill the time. You can enjoy highlights, food and wine tastings, organized activities and time at the spa, pool or casino.

    According to recent reports, many repositioning crossings are relatively smooth, and modern ships use stabilizers to reduce movement. But since these itineraries cross open ocean rather than staying closer to land, there can be more motion, especially on North Atlantic crossings in fall and winter.

    If you tend to get seasick, this could be a dealbreaker. Even if a repositioning sailing is smooth, temperatures can be chilly on the open ocean, especially on northerly or spring and fall transatlantic routes, with strong winds that may make suntanning by the pool less appealing.

    Industry observers note that you can book one of these sailings in the same way you would book a traditional cruise. But if you’re searching for dates and itineraries on a cruise line’s website, they may be listed as transatlantic, transpacific or Panama Canal sailings rather than repositioning cruises, though some lines do use the term "repositioning." There’s even a website that specializes in rounding up these cruises: RepoCruises.com.

    Sources indicate that keep an eye out for themed sailings that focus on topics like wine, theater or music, where fellow guests on the ship may share similar interests. Cruise lines often schedule them on repositioning cruises to spur demand.

    Here are some repositioning cruises for 2027. They often take place during shoulder seasons, between the most popular cruising times in places like the Mediterranean or Caribbean.

    According to recent reports, this journey repositions the ship from Miami, where it sails on Caribbean itineraries, to Seattle, where it will visit ports in Alaska during the spring and summer months. Departing April 8, 2027, the 18-night cruise includes stops at various ports in Colombia, Panama and Mexico, as well as San Diego and Los Angeles, before arriving in Seattle on April 26.

    Regent Seven Seas Cruises' all-suite luxury ship Seven Seas Mariner will sail between Latest York and Lisbon, making stops in Canada, Morocco and the Portuguese islands of Madeira and the Azores.

    Departing April 29, 2027, the 16-night journey ends in Lisbon, Portugal, as the ship repositions to Europe, where it will sail various itineraries, including Mediterranean sailings later in the summer season.

    Departing Seattle on Sept. 28, 2027, Norwegian Jade will sail to Yokohama, Japan, with stops in Alaska and northern Japan. This is a way to travel across the Pacific with less jet lag, since the journey takes place over several days, with ship clocks typically adjusted gradually (often an hour at a time) during the sailing. Note that the voyage also crosses the International Date Line.

    Recent findings suggest that if Greenland has been on your bucket list, this 16-night sailing is a way to get up close and personal with its natural scenery. Departing Reykjavik on Aug. 25, 2027, Azamara Quest will sail from Iceland to the U.S. It will make stops in Greenland, Canada and Latest England before reaching the Massive Apple.

    Departing Bergen, Norway, on June 11, 2027, this 28-night sailing aboard Viking Vela sails around Iceland's coast, makes two stops in Greenland and crosses the Atlantic before reaching Upcoming York.

    #165314. The Buffett Indicator Is More Than 70 Points Above Its Dot-Com Peak. Here’s What That Means for Long-Term Investors.

    📅 24 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 4m • 📚 Deep Dive (766 w)
    📖 Baca
    General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Fool ↗ Open Full Page

    The Buffett Indicator Is More Than 70 Points Above Its Dot-Com Peak. Here’s What That Means for Long-Term Investors.

    📅 24 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (766 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Fool

    ⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Sources indicate that in a 2001 Fortune article, Warren Buffett publicly mentioned the idea of gauging the stock market's valuation by comparing the country's total equity market capitalization to its GDP.
    • Industry observers note that before that, at the dot-com peak in the spring of 2000, the Buffett indicator was just under 150%.
    • Relative to what was going on at the turn of the century, the current Buffett indicator of 222%, more than 70 percentage points above the dot-com record, is in the stratosphere.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    By Neil Patel – Nov 24, 2026 at 4:45AM EST.

    10 stocks we like better than S&P 500 Index ›.

    Sources indicate that in a 2001 Fortune article, Warren Buffett publicly mentioned the idea of gauging the stock market's valuation by comparing the country's total equity market capitalization to its GDP. This concept was introduced just after the technology bubble burst.

    Industry observers note that before that, at the dot-com peak in the spring of 2000, the Buffett indicator was just under 150%. This was a level that suggested the stock market was extremely overvalued. That proved to be the correct view; Over the following decade, the S&P 500 (^GSPC +4.73%) produced a negative single-digit total return.

    Relative to what was going on at the turn of the century, the current Buffett indicator of 222%, more than 70 percentage points above the dot-com record, is in the stratosphere. It's not far off the highest reading ever from three months ago in August. Investors have definitely been concerned.

    Here's how to interpret the Buffett indicator as 2026 nears its end.

    If you perfectly mistimed your investment allocation and bought an S&P 500 exchange-traded fund, such as the SPDR S&P 500 ETF Trust (SPY +4.71%) in early 2000 when the Buffett indicator was around 150%, as mentioned, your portfolio suffered by losing money in the subsequent decade. The stock market was performing well prior to the housing market meltdown, however, a generational event that led to a severe economic crisis. It's impossible to have predicted this would happen.

    Industry observers note that nonetheless, investors might be skeptical that buying stocks is the right move today. With the Buffett indicator at 222%, what does this mean for the equity market over the next 10 years?

    All else equal, history says that high starting valuations result in lower forward returns. The tech bubble is the clearest example. This is true even though past trends aren't guaranteed to repeat.

    Sources indicate that according to research from J.P. Morgan (JPM +1.97%) Asset Management, the bank believes that U.S. large-cap stocks will produce an annualized total return of 7.5% in the next 10 to 15 years. That's not alarming, but it's significantly below the 14.7% yearly pace of the prior decade (as of Nov. 18). And considering above-normal inflation, the real projected return is lower.

    Sources indicate that but investors should understand the Buffett indicator's limitations. It ignores revenues that businesses collect outside the U.S., as this doesn't get captured in the GDP figure that's in the denominator. The biggest companies, especially those that operate in the technology sector, have substantial foreign operations, which naturally skews the Buffett indicator higher.

    It has been revealed that investors shouldn't be deterred. The right response to this information is still to build a diversified portfolio. If you can't help but be worried, then maybe it's best to increase your cash position. This will enable you to take advantage of opportunities that come up. And of course, always focus on buying high-quality names.

    According to recent reports, if you're someone who's staring at a multi-decade time horizon until retirement, it's recommended that you stay optimistic and bullish over the long term. Over any 20-year rolling period, the S&P 500 index has generated a positive return.

    Waiting for a cheaper valuation seems like the right move. However, you shouldn't try to time the market. When the Buffett indicator was first thought of, a reading over 120% might have been considered expensive. Today, it's plausible that a Buffett indicator of over 200% is normal.

    Industry observers note that the nature of the monetary landscape is worth exploring. Since 2000, the M2 money supply in the U.S. has ballooned more than 400%. Furthermore, the U.S. federal debt has increased 7x during that same period. I think these are underappreciated tailwinds. There's no way that all of this liquidity, which supports risk assets and nominal earnings growth, hasn't had a profound impact on the stock market. Looking ahead, that trend will continue to be a constant propellant.

    Be mindful of the Buffett indicator. But don't let it distract you. Time should continue to work in long-term investors' favor.

    The Perpetual Futures Market Is Booming. That Might Not Be as Bullish for Hyperliquid as Some Investors Think.

    📅 24 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (786 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Fool

    💡 Key Takeaways
    • The perpetual futures boom will probably continue to be great for the business of Hyperliquid (HYPE -1.91%), but it's also luring an entire roster of well-funded rivals that will be sharply contesting its advance every step of the way.
    • In a recent development, it's true that a growing perpetual futures market could present the opportunity for yet another clean win for its leaders.
    • Here's which players are in the competitive landscape right now, and how much they might threaten Hyperliquid down the line.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    By Alex Carchidi – Nov 24, 2026 at 4:50AM EST.

    10 stocks we like better than Hyperliquid ›.

    The perpetual futures boom will probably continue to be great for the business of Hyperliquid (HYPE -1.91%), but it's also luring an entire roster of well-funded rivals that will be sharply contesting its advance every step of the way. On Nov. 18, CoinDesk reported that one emerging challenger, Variational, raised $110 million in capital at a $1.5 billion valuation to target Hyperliquid's loyal customer base and future prospects. It plans to launch its own token, VAR, before the end of 2026.

    In a recent development, it's true that a growing perpetual futures market could present the opportunity for yet another clean win for its leaders. But rivals like Robinhood Markets (HOOD +8.36%) and Coinbase Global (COIN +6.68%) already have millions of customers, while Hyperliquid and its smaller peers need to convert new customers one wallet at a time.

    Here's which players are in the competitive landscape right now, and how much they might threaten Hyperliquid down the line.

    Among decentralized exchanges (DEXs), which execute trades on a public blockchain rather than through an intermediary, Hyperliquid's lead is lopsided.

    As of Nov. 23, it received  72% of the fees generated by all DEXes, with $2.7 million for that 24-hour period, compared to its smaller competitors Aster (ASTER -2.63%), which only brought in about $102,500, and $146,400 for Lighter (LIT -1.36%)in the same period.

    CRYPTO · As of 6:49 AM ET 11/24/26.

    Centralized platforms with a strong presence in the traditional financial sector are the bigger threat by far, as they're guaranteed to have both large user bases and ample capital of their own to deploy as they contest the market. Hyperliquid's $718.7 billion in volume in the third quarter of 2026 was only 69% of Robinhood's volume of about $1 trillion.

    According to recent reports, in May, the Commodity Futures Trading Commission (CFTC) cleared Coinbase to list crypto perpetuals, and on Sept. 29, Robinhood said it would offer U.S. perps in the coming months at a commission of 0.01% per trade through the end of the year. Robinhood had 28.7 million customers with funded accounts as of the end of the third quarter, and Coinbase had 7.4 million monthly people who made transactions that quarter. In contrast, Hyperliquid has voluntarily made itself off-limits to Americans in advance of securing regulatory permission to operate in the U.S., and it's not clear what the status of seeking or attaining that permission is as of late November.

    Importantly, Robinhood has also chosen a decentralized exchange as its favorite, meaning it can erode Hyperliquid's market share from two directions. Its venture arm has backed Lighter, and outside the U.S., its wallet app sends owners to Lighter's perpetuals.

    In other words, the customers who could fuel the next legs of the perpetuals boom mostly belong to someone other than Hyperliquid. And its centralized competitors also have platforms that are significantly easier to start using, as they can leverage their traditional financial infrastructure to eliminate the need to fund a latest crypto wallet and transfer funds into it, as on Hyperliquid.

    Hyperliquid has some allies in its corner, too.

    Recent findings suggest that on Sept. 16, the Kraken crypto exchange's parent company, Payward, said it planned to list Hyperliquid-based perpetuals for its U.S. clients, pending regulatory approval. Payward had 6.6 million funded accounts as of June 30, so Hyperliquid could be positioned to settle a good amount of additional trading activity, which would boost the price of its HYPE coin by way of converting its transaction fees into buybacks of its token.

    However, that access to Payward's user base comes at a cost of its own, which might prove troublesome. Customers of markets built by outside operators, as Payward's would be, need to pay roughly double Hyperliquid's normal fees. Pricier contracts are a tough sell next to Robinhood's promotional rates.

    Hyperliquid is still worth buying for risk-tolerant investors with a multiyear holding horizon, but it's no longer the only big fish in the perpetuals pond. Of course, perps aren't its only line of business -- it also offers prediction markets, spot trading, and other revenue-generating features too -- so it will likely be resilient even if it has to fight harder to advance.

    #165303. Switching ERPs Without The Consulting Army

    📅 24 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 5m • 📚 Deep Dive (1038 w)
    📖 Baca
    General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Forbes ↗ Open Full Page

    Switching ERPs Without The Consulting Army

    📅 24 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (1038 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Forbes

    ⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • For decades, replacing an enterprise resource planning (ERP) system has meant systems integrators, functional consultants, migration specialists, developers, months of workshops, mapping spreadsheets, testing and reconciliation.
    • Yet, much of this work follows a predictable pattern:​ discover, profile, map, transform, validate, load, reconcile and, finally, approve.​.
    • That is where AI can change ERP implementation economics.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Deepak Padgaonkar, founding member of V3iT.

    For decades, replacing an enterprise resource planning (ERP) system has meant systems integrators, functional consultants, migration specialists, developers, months of workshops, mapping spreadsheets, testing and reconciliation.

    Yet, much of this work follows a predictable pattern:​ discover, profile, map, transform, validate, load, reconcile and, finally, approve.​.

    That is where AI can change ERP implementation economics.

    Recent findings suggest that the future is not a completely autonomous ERP project. It is a small implementation team supervising an AI-driven migration factory instead of a consulting army manually performing every step.

    SAP provides the S/4HANA Migration Cockpit, including migration objects and staging mechanisms. Microsoft Dynamics 365 provides its Data Management Framework, with reusable data entities for customers, vendors, products, orders and balances. NetSuite supports migration through CSV imports and SuiteCloud/REST interfaces.

    AI-assisted migration tools are beginning to approach the problem differently. Platforms such as TRANXACT.AI, use AI to connect to source systems, map data and support migration through a pipeline that can run alongside existing systems. The broader trend is toward treating migration as a continuous data-management process rather than a one-time conversion project.

    Rather than replace migration technology, the opportunity is to put an AI orchestration, reasoning and reconciliation layer around it. That layer matters because loading data is the easy part; deciding what the data should become is not. Captured as reviewable rules, it can be tested, reused and audited, and the CIO’s question shifts from how many people a migration needs to how well its decisions are governed. ​.

    It has been revealed that imagine connecting the legacy and target ERPs to an AI orchestration layer. Instead of hundreds of hours of discovery and spreadsheets, AI inventories source structures and compares them with target APIs, migration objects and data entities.

    It has been revealed that consider a hypothetical: A legacy system stores a payment term as one code, and the latest system expects another. Instead of someone fixing it row by row in a spreadsheet, AI recognizes the pattern and proposes a rule.

    Recent findings suggest that A human approves the rule once; it is applied across thousands of records. ​.

    Where AI is uncertain, such as with an ambiguous ledger account, it routes the decision to someone qualified to make it. The model changes from humans mapping everything to humans reviewing exceptions and approving rules. ​.

    Recent findings suggest that consider moving from 2,400 legacy GL accounts to a redesigned chart of 1,100. AI can analyze descriptions, historical postings, cost centers and account types to propose mappings while routing uncertain decisions to the controller.

    More importantly, reconciliation becomes continuous.

    If the two systems agree on assets, but differ between liabilities and equity, AI can trace the variance to the postings and mapping rule behind it and propose a correction.

    The question changes from “Why don’t the systems reconcile?” to “Do we approve this correction?” ​.

    In a recent development, that matters for financial controls. Continuous reconciliation catches errors while they are small and their cause is obvious. Every mapping, correction and approval is recorded with its rationale, giving auditors a documented trail. And oversight sharpens rather than disappears: Controllers stay accountable, with explicit approval rights, thresholds and segregation of duties.

    Whatever tool they choose, buyers should insist on continuous reconciliation across every period and subledger, proposals a finance user can understand, traceability from source record to target, human approval of accounting treatment and results that can be verified independently of the tool that produced them.​.

    An opening-balance migration moves master data, GL balances, open receivables and payables, inventory, fixed assets and open orders while historical transactions remain archived.

    A historical migration might bring one, three or five years of detail, with AI analyzing dependencies, sequencing loads, identifying missing references and reconciling results.

    For many companies, a hybrid makes sense:.

    • Current And Prior Year: transaction detail• Years 3–7: summarized monthly balances• Older History: analytical archive• Open Documents: individually migrated• Master Data: fully migrated.

    This provides useful history without reproducing decades of legacy complexity.

    Where to draw those lines depends on regulatory and tax retention rules, management’s need for multiyear transaction-level reporting, the quality of older data, the cost of converting and reconciling each additional year, performance in the new system and auditors’ access to archived records.

    A useful rule: Move what the business needs to operate, archive what it must retain and leave the rest.​.

    An AI-driven migration factory profiles transactions, proposes account mappings, detects duplicates, generates transformation rules, identifies invalid data, executes approved loads, compares balances and produces reconciliation evidence.

    Humans concentrate on judgment. Should these accounts be consolidated? Which duplicate vendor is authoritative? Is the accounting treatment correct? Is the reconciliation acceptable? Are we ready to go live?

    It has been revealed that AI does not eliminate ERP expertise. It reduces repetitive migration labor while preserving human control over accounting, configuration, compliance and business decisions.

    In a recent development, the conventional model scales by adding people. An AI migration factory scales through connectors, mappings, validation rules, reconciliation agents and exception management.

    Recent findings suggest that the implementation team does not disappear. It gets smaller and more specialized.

    Recent findings suggest that firms and IT teams will need to adapt. The most valuable skills will blend accounting, process knowledge and data governance with the ability to supervise automation. Billable-headcount consulting will give way to smaller senior teams and outcome-based pricing.

    Recent findings suggest that upcoming risks emerge, too: over-trusted confidence scores, flawed rules propagating at scale and knowledge concentrated in too few people. Sampling auto-approved work and validating independently before cutover become essential. ​.

    Recent findings suggest that for 30 years, companies bought sophisticated ERP software and hired armies of people to move their businesses into it. The next generation is reversing that relationship: the software is increasingly helping to move the business itself.

    ERP migration will never be entirely mechanical, but extracting 22 million ledger lines, proposing mappings, loading approved data, reconciling systems and identifying the 37 transactions that do not match? More and more, there is little reason for humans to spend thousands of hours doing that manually.​.

    Forbes Technology Council is an invitation-only community for world-class CIOs, CTOs and technology executives. Do I qualify?

    By Adam Levy – Nov 24, 2026 at 4:55AM EST.

    10 stocks we like better than Nvidia ›.

    It has been revealed that nvidia's (NVDA +31.48%) earnings report last week, without Jensen Huang leading the tech giant, went better than expected. Revenue climbed 103% year over year to $115.8 billion, and earnings per share climbed to $2.70, up 108%. Both came in above analysts' expectations.

    Perhaps more crucial was CFO and interim CEO Colette Kress's fiscal 2028 guidance. Last quarter she said she expects 70% revenue growth. This quarter, she increased it to 75%. That's despite higher-than-expected revenue growth last quarter and strong fourth-quarter guidance.

    Her fourth-quarter guidance calls for $130 billion in revenue, bringing fiscal 2027 total revenue to $423.7 billion. A 75% growth rate implies $741 billion in revenue next year. Here's what that means for the stock.

    With the recent sell-off in shares, the company has a market cap of about $4 trillion as of this writing. That means the stock is priced just over 5 times next year's sales. Its stock price has dropped to 10 times analysts' expectations for next year's earnings.

    There are a few reasons why a stock would be so cheap.

    Kress looked to put investors at ease during the earnings call. She remarked her 75% revenue growth outlook is based on "data center readiness, the strength and durability of end customer demand, and our customers' access to capital." She noted the $32 billion in financial commitments to neocloud companies require those partners to secure their own capital for data centers first. She stressed that Nvidia has a multi-year roadmap in place and it's "business as usual.".

    NASDAQ · As of 4:00 PM ET 11/23/26.

    While Nvidia shares look incredibly cheap right now, there's a lot of uncertainty about the business. While Huang has been reinstated as CEO, investors need to know whether he knowingly or unknowingly sold chips that ultimately landed in China, and what percentage of Nvidia's sales they accounted for. There could be legal repercussions as well, in the form of fines and further sales restrictions, which would impact Nvidia's bottom line.

    Sources indicate that nvidia is also increasingly reliant on neocloud companies continuing to build swiftly, a trend that faces both regulatory and credit risks. While Nvidia's GPUs remain best-in-class and can remain so even without Huang, the risk is that hyperscalers and leading AI labs will run more of their software on custom silicon instead of GPUs.

    To be sure, the market appears to be pricing in the risks to Nvidia at the current price. But there are other AI stocks that have been caught up in the broader AI sell-off and look like great opportunities with less uncertainty. For now, a wait-and-see approach may be most prudent for Nvidia stock.

    #165299. Industry News: AI Agents And Ontology: Why Data Access Is Not Enough

    📅 24 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 4m • 📚 Deep Dive (770 w)
    📖 Baca
    AI & Tech ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Forbes ↗ Open Full Page

    Industry News: AI Agents And Ontology: Why Data Access Is Not Enough

    📅 24 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (770 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Forbes

    ⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Mohan Shekar is VP at SAP, driving enterprise AI adoption, with a focus on emerging computing technologies.
    • It has been revealed that ​For decades, CIOs have managed technical debt, including aging applications and expensive workarounds.
    • Consider a manufacturer whose CRM marks a customer as a strategic account.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Mohan Shekar is VP at SAP, driving enterprise AI adoption, with a focus on emerging computing technologies.

    It has been revealed that ​For decades, CIOs have managed technical debt, including aging applications and expensive workarounds. AI agents are now exposing a second liability that has built up alongside it: semantic debt. This is the accumulated cost of inconsistent business definitions and unwritten rules, the things experienced employees navigate by instinct but software cannot reliably infer.

    Consider a manufacturer whose CRM marks a customer as a strategic account. Its ERP records several legal entities under that relationship. Its finance system flags an overdue invoice against one of them and an agent asked to release a delayed order can retrieve all three records. Yet retrieving those records does not necessarily answer the critical questions: Which entity signed the contract? Does that invoice block this shipment? Who can approve an exception?

    According to recent reports, if the agent guesses wrong, it could hold an order the business wanted shipped or ship one finance would have stopped. The data was available, but the meaning was not.

    Master data management and integration platforms have improved consistency and access for years. Conventional workflows often rely on business definitions and rules settled during design. A shipment-blocking workflow, for example, follows a predefined interpretation of a particular credit status.

    Recent findings suggest that agents encounter ambiguity dynamically, across systems, while deciding what to do next. Handling an unfamiliar exception, an agent must identify the right entity, find the governing contract, interpret a credit policy and route a proposal to the right approver. Each step depends on relationships that may be familiar to an experienced employee but unclear across applications.

    What has changed is that AI agents are beginning to act on business meanings that organizations have not consistently reconciled across systems. Before blaming the model, leaders should ask whether the relevant business rule, and the system authorized to define it, has been made explicit. More connectors may simply deliver conflicting answers faster.

    Recent findings suggest that an ontology is an explicit model of business concepts, their relationships and, where needed, their constraints. It can state that an account belongs to a legal entity, that the entity is party to a contract and that a credit policy applies to certain orders. Combined with trustworthy data, it helps establish which records and rules belong together.

    But not every agent needs a formal enterprise ontology. Clean APIs, reliable data and explicit rules may be enough, and even a complex agent may gain more from repaired master data than from another modeling platform.

    It helps to keep four layers distinct:.

    Recent findings suggest that an agent can understand an exception perfectly and still lack the authority to approve it. Confusing these layers is how organizations end up funding the wrong fix.

    In a recent development, vendors’ models encode deep domain knowledge and often work well within their own systems. The trouble is at the boundaries: An enterprise running agents across platforms cannot assume they define customer, supplier, obligation or approval the same way, or that those meanings reconcile cheaply.

    Recent findings suggest that CIOs can rely on each vendor’s semantics, build a centrally governed enterprise model or federate definitions across domains. Federation offers a practical starting point: Finance stays authoritative for financial obligations, sales for customer relationships and procurement for supplier classifications, with cross-domain relationships documented where agents need them. That ownership cannot sit with IT alone. Business leaders define what terms and policies mean; technology teams make those definitions accessible and testable.

    Start with one consequential workflow, such as order release or claims resolution, and measure how often agents select the wrong entity, miss an applicable rule, need human correction or produce a decision no one can explain.

    Then compare fixes: cleaner master data, clearer APIs, deterministic rules or an explicit relationship model. Evaluate the reduction in errors alongside the cost of keeping each solution current. The goal is the lowest sustainable cost of correct business interpretation.

    In a recent development, making business relationships explicit is necessary but not sufficient. Once agents act on those definitions, they become operational infrastructure: They must be versioned, tested against real decisions, governed as controls and updated when policies change. An ontology nobody maintains becomes semantic debt of its own.

    So beyond choosing who supplies their agents, CIOs need to decide who owns the meaning those agents rely on and whether that meaning holds when an agent crosses from one system to the next.

    By Thomas Niel – Nov 24, 2026 at 5:00AM EST.

    10 stocks we like better than Brookfield Corporation ›.

    Recent findings suggest that next week, Canadian asset management and holding manufacturer Brookfield Corporation (BN +3.63%) prepares to complete a consolidation transaction to simplify its complex business structure. On Dec. 1, Brookfield will combine with Brookfield Wealth Solutions (BNT +3.82%), or BWS for short.

    Recent findings suggest that management has high hopes for the combination, which will result in an entity known as Brookfield Corporation Ltd. Still, this combination may not achieve an objective shareholders may want addressed as soon as possible: closing the valuation gap between the stock and the firm's underlying per-share value.

    Brookfield Corporation has long had a complex organizational structure. Not only does the firm have multiple publicly traded, majority-owned subsidiaries, such as Brookfield Asset Management (BAM +2.19%), but Brookfield also at the moment holds full economic interest in BWS, which is domiciled in Bermuda. The Bermuda-based entity is also publicly traded, but its shares have always been exchangeable for shares in Canadian-domiciled Brookfield Corporation.

    NYSE · As of 4:00 PM ET 11/23/26.

    However, this is changing at the start of next month. Per a proposed transaction approved by shareholders last summer, Brookfield Corporation and BWS agreed to merge into a newly introduced Bermuda-based holding firm, Brookfield Corporation Ltd. This company will continue to trade on the Toronto Stock Exchange (TSX) and the New York Stock Exchange (NYSE) under the ticker symbol "BN.".

    In a recent development, completing this transaction could bring numerous benefits. For one, combining the two entities enables direct access to the former Brookfield Corporation's permanent capital base. Because the deal also helps to increase the stock's free float outstanding, the shares could benefit from future index inclusion. However, Brookfield's corporate structure will stay largely opaque, which may make it difficult for the firm to make any progress eliminating the challenges that have long made it a value stock.

    Recent findings suggest that last year, Brookfield's management estimated that the stock's underlying value was $68 per share, almost 75% higher than recent prices. Furthermore, management expressed its belief that continued growth of Brookfield's asset management and insurance businesses, coupled with investment returns on its permanent capital, could result in the stock's underlying value reaching $140 per share by 2030.

    In a recent development, however, since this projection, Brookfield Corporation shares have pulled back. In my view, this valuation gap still exists for two reasons. First, much of Brookfield's value comes from its 73% stake in Brookfield Asset Management. It's common for Wall Street to apply a discount to holding companies with complex structures. A further simplification, like a full consolidation of Brookfield Asset Management into Brookfield Corporation Ltd., may be necessary to close the valuation gap.

    Industry observers note that management's estimate also includes the value of Brookfield's other holdings in publicly traded and privately held investment entities, including the net present value of its carried interest, or profit based on the performance of its investments. In addition, given Brookfield's high exposure to areas like private credit and AI data centers, investors could also be factoring in the potential for the respective booms in either area to give way to a slowdown, or worse, a meltdown.

    It has been revealed that brookfield appears to be a solid value opportunity among financial stocks, although patience is necessary. With impending changes that may mark just the start of further simplification in the years ahead, the stock could rise as investors become more confident in management's valuation argument.

However, bond prices for several neoclouds and hyperscalers have plunged throughout the year, including Nvidia, whose 2060 notes have hit record lows.     Here's how the brokerage performed in its quarter ended Sept. 30, compared with Wall Street estimates, based on a survey of analysts by LSEG:.

    Industry observers note that robinhood's net income fell to $468 million, or 51 cents per share, from $556 million, or 61 cents per share, a year ago. Revenue represented a 12% increase from $1.27 billion in the same quarter last year.

    Despite that gain, transaction-based revenue of $867 million came in below Wall Street estimates from StreetAccount of $879 million, putting focus on whether Robinhood can sustain momentum across its trading businesses and reduce its reliance on volatile market activity.

    It has been revealed that robinhood has been diversifying its business as it tries to expand its brokerage app into a broader financial services platform. Options trading and event contracts have become increasingly important sources of transaction revenue, while the organization has continued to invest in wealth management, subscriptions and other offerings.

    Industry observers note that transaction-based revenue grew 19% from the same period last year to $867 million, driven primarily by a more than 500% increase in event contracts revenue. Additionally, options revenue grew 31% to $399 million and equities revenue rose 41% to $121 million.

    Those gains were partially offset by cryptocurrency revenue, which fell 55% to $120 million.

    Chief Financial Officer Shiv Verma told CNBC event contracts on crypto movements did well in the quarter, offering investors another way to express a view on crypto despite the slump in prices and spot trading.

    Industry observers note that net deposits on the Robinhood platform totaled $15.7 billion for the quarter, equal to a 17% annualized growth rate based on total platform assets at the end of Q2 2026. Over the past year, net deposits totaled $71 billion, representing 21% growth compared with total platform assets at the end of Q3 2025.

    According to recent reports, nvidia (NVDA +31.48%) is the bellwether for the artificial intelligence (AI) industry, and for CoreWeave (CRWV +22.32%), it's even more. The former is an AI chip giant, and the latter is a neocloud tech giant, offering customers access to such chips. Nvidia has played a key role in CoreWeave's growth, with support including stock purchases, revenue guarantees, and credit backing.

    All of this helped CoreWeave's shares climb in its early months of trading last year. Though the stock gave up some gains from its market debut, it continued to offer those early investors positive performance all the way through last month. But in recent weeks, general concern about a tighter credit market and the pace of the AI build-out weighed on CoreWeave and peers. Then troubles at key partner Nvidia added to the pressure.

    Nvidia chief Jensen Huang stepped down earlier this month following allegations of affairs, then was reinstated earlier this week. Amid the turmoil at Nvidia, how big is the risk for CoreWeave? Let's find out.

    First, let's take a closer look at the Nvidia-CoreWeave relationship and consider what's at stake. As mentioned, CoreWeave offers AI chips, but not just any. The company works exclusively with Nvidia and has even been the first cloud provider to make Nvidia's latest updates generally available. CoreWeave offers its customers a fleet of Nvidia's graphics processing units (GPUs) that they can rent for short or long periods of time to run their workloads, and demand has been soaring. In the recent quarter, CoreWeave reported a 168% increase in revenue to $3.6 billion.

    Industry observers note that nvidia has been a strong supporter of this young AI manufacturer, starting with its 10% stake in CoreWeave. The tech giant owns more than 47 million CoreWeave shares, making it the third-largest position in Nvidia's investment portfolio. Nvidia has also pledged revenue support; for example, it's agreed to purchase any unused capacity through April 2032. Nvidia, thanks to its solid credit rating, has acted as a backstop for CoreWeave as it seeks borrowings to build out. And Nvidia has also funded companies that then turn to CoreWeave for access to chips.

    NASDAQ · As of 4:00 PM ET 11/23/26.

    It has been revealed that however, with investors keenly focused on Nvidia’s financing support for neoclouds, the situation moving forward could become more difficult for these AI cloud specialists. During Huang’s brief departure, Nvidia finance chief Colette Kress stated that financial guarantees for neocloud agreements depend on those companies' ability to secure their own capital for the build-out.

    At the same time, Nvidia faces headwinds that may shift its focus somewhat in the coming months. The organization is investigating an alleged spy effort that targeted Jensen Huang. And, separately, press reports say the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission has introduced a probe concerning Nvidia’s accounting practices.

    CoreWeave, however, may not be as dependent on Nvidia’s attention to its financial situation as we might have thought. CoreWeave offered a positive message in its earnings call, saying, “Our growth is supported by multiple sources of funding, including financing backed by customer contracts, operating cash flow, and approximately $9 billion in customer prepayments and deposits expected in the next three months alone.”.

    And Jensen Huang early last month expressed confidence in CoreWeave’s financial position.

    Sources indicate that so, considering all of this, how big of a risk is the Nvidia turmoil for CoreWeave? I think any potential Nvidia challenges could weigh on appetite for CoreWeave stock due to the companies’ close relations.

    CoreWeave is a highly leveraged firm, with most of its build-out funded by debt.

    CRWV Debt to Equity Ratio data by YCharts.

    In a recent development, this, too, may represent a headwind today as investors worry about the sustainability of AI spending on AI infrastructure. And as Democrats take leadership in the House and Senate early next year, this feeling may intensify. Democratic leaders have been known for a cautious approach when it comes to developing AI.

    Industry observers note that all of this means that CoreWeave, amid current uncertainty and its dependence on Nvidia, carries significant risk. It's crucial to keep an eye on Nvidia's comments regarding neoclouds in the months to come — even if CoreWeave has gained financial strength, investors still feel reassured by Nvidia’s support. It will also be vital to monitor messages from the government about the AI build-out to get a better idea of what's next for CoreWeave.

    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Investors shouldn't label Walmart (WMT +1.27%) a slow-moving and outdated retail enterprise.
    • Industry observers note that walmart's fiscal 2027 third-quarter (ended Oct.
    • The retail stock's scale is the highlight.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    By Neil Patel – Nov 24, 2026 at 5:20AM EST.

    10 stocks we like better than Walmart ›.

    Investors shouldn't label Walmart (WMT +1.27%) a slow-moving and outdated retail enterprise. The business is performing well in today's internet-driven economy. And it reveals. Shares generated a market-thumping total return of 154% in the past three years (as of Nov. 19).

    Industry observers note that walmart's fiscal 2027 third-quarter (ended Oct. 31) financial results were very encouraging. It beat analyst estimates on the top and bottom lines. And following last quarter's renewed outlook, management once again raised sales and profit guidance. This is a positive trend as the critical holiday shopping period is upon us.

    The retail stock's scale is the highlight. Here are three numbers that show why this key competitive advantage continues to grow.

    Recent findings suggest that the first number is 23%. That's how fast Walmart's U.S. e-commerce sales grew in the third quarter. By comparison, Walmart's U.S. comparable sales, which measure growth at stores and digital channels open at least a year, rose 2.9% (excluding fuel).

    This might come as a surprise. After all, Amazon (AMZN +3.47%) wrote the online retail playbook, and it dominates online shopping.

    But Walmart has something the e-commerce giant can't easily copy. Its 5,200 domestic stores sit within 10 miles of 90% of the U.S. population. Many of those sites were secured decades ago. Today, they double as delivery hubs.

    Sources indicate that that creates density for the logistics network. More orders flowing through the same buildings and trucks means a lower cost per package. And Walmart can spread its heavy investments in automation over hundreds of billions of dollars in annual sales. That's hard to compete with.

    Industry observers note that walmart U.S. advertising revenue jumped 37% in the third quarter. This is where scale starts paying a second dividend. And it reveals the business is leaning into the advantage that its data offers.

    Recent findings suggest that walmart Connect, the organization's ads platform, sells brand placements across its website, app, and stores. The pitch is simple. Walmart knows what 150 million weekly U.S. shoppers actually buy, not just what they click on. Brands want to reach those intentional shoppers at the moment of purchase.

    Sources indicate that there's a positive feedback loop here. Walmart's massive revenue base gives it negotiating leverage with suppliers. That leverage helps keep prices low, which drives customer traffic. And traffic is exactly what advertisers pay for.

    Industry observers note that the economics are exceptional. The audience and infrastructure already exist, so each additional ad dollar costs little to bring in, leading to "over 70% margins," according to Walmart Connect senior vice president Ryan Mayward. Groceries, by contrast, are a low-margin business. Ad revenue has a much bigger positive impact on the bottom line.

    NASDAQ · As of 4:00 PM ET 11/23/26.

    Recent findings suggest that global membership fee revenue grew 17%. This includes Sam's Club membership fees and Walmart+, the company's subscription service that goes head-to-head with Amazon Prime and offers free delivery and other benefits.

    Membership fees are recurring and high-margin. Customers pay up front, and Walmart's job is to make that fee feel like a bargain. Its lean supply chain helps to make that possible. Low operating costs allow the organization to bundle perks such as free delivery, streaming, and discounts without giving up its price advantage.

    In a recent development, that changes shopping behavior. People will favor spending with a retailer they've already paid, and members spend four times more than non-members. More spending makes Walmart larger. A larger Walmart negotiates better prices. And these better prices attract more members.

    This is every retailer's dream. A paid membership program can only work if the value proposition is strong enough. Walmart's everyday low prices lay the foundation.

    Put these three numbers together, and the quarter's most important figure comes into focus. Reported operating income rose 5.5% (on a constant-currency basis), faster than revenue. Over the past three years, adjusted operating income climbed 24%, while sales were up 17%.

    According to recent reports, walmart's success in e-commerce, advertising, and memberships is a tailwind. Shareholders should watch whether profits keep outgrowing revenue. This would indicate that the scale-based flywheel is still working.

    Marvell Stock Fell Almost 12% in a Single Day. I'd Consider Buying Shares Now.

    📅 24 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (868 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Fool

    ⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • 10 stocks we like better than Marvell Technology ›.
    • Recent findings suggest that marvell Technology (MRVL +18.37%) stock fell almost 12% on Nov.
    • Most of that slide happened over the past month.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    By Daniel Sparks – Nov 24, 2026 at 5:37AM EST.

    10 stocks we like better than Marvell Technology ›.

    Recent findings suggest that marvell Technology (MRVL +18.37%) stock fell almost 12% on Nov. 20 to close at $122.28. The chipmaker's shares hadn't closed this low since April. And they stood at around 39% of the record close they hit on June 4 -- $316.43.

    Most of that slide happened over the past month. Marvell closed around $252 on Oct. 28, the last trading day before news broke that it was in talks to buy optical parts maker Lumentum Holdings (LITE +18.20%). The stock had lost over half its value by Nov. 20.

    Shares rebounded sharply on Nov. 23, but I think the sell-off has still gone further than the business justifies. At this price, the stock is valued as if Marvell's growth was about to fade into something ordinary. Its data center business is doing the opposite, so I'd buy the shares now.

    Sources indicate that data centers account for most of Marvell's sales. They made up 79% of its revenue in the fiscal second quarter of 2027 (the period ended Aug. 1, 2026).

    Industry observers note that showing how promptly demand has picked up, Marvell's data center revenue reached around $2.17 billion in fiscal Q2, up 46% year over year. That was faster than the 27% growth in fiscal Q1 and the 21% growth in the fourth quarter of fiscal 2026. Plus, management guided for data center revenue to grow around 75% from a year earlier in the fiscal third quarter, which ended Oct. 31. And profits are keeping up with sales. Marvell's non-GAAP (adjusted) earnings per share climbed 40% year over year in fiscal Q2.

    Sources indicate that the fourth-quarter report, released in March, was still Marvell's latest earnings revision the last time the stock closed this low, on April 9. Since then, the data center business has moved from 21% growth to a guided 75%, but the share price has landed right back near where it was.

    Marvell's data center business brought in around $2.2 billion for all of fiscal 2024. In fiscal Q2 alone, it brought in almost as much.

    According to recent reports, marvell reports fiscal third-quarter results on Dec. 1, which will show if data center sales met that guide. But on Nov. 2, the company said preliminary total revenue for the quarter was consistent with its guidance.

    At around $146, Marvell's price-to-earnings ratio is about 20 using the adjusted per-share earnings analysts expect for fiscal 2028 (it ends in January 2028). For comparison, FactSet puts the forward price-to-earnings ratio of the S&P 500 at about 17, based on expected earnings for the next 12 months. Marvell's fiscal 2028 goes a few months further out than that period, but the two multiples are not far apart.

    So investors are now paying only a little more than a market-average price for Marvell's expected earnings.

    According to recent reports, marvell's own blueprint for fiscal 2028 is far from average. Management's outlook, given at an Oct. 6 investor day, calls for around $20 billion in revenue that year. That would be about 67% above the roughly $12 billion it expects this fiscal year. I'd expect a market-average price for a company whose growth was slowing, not accelerating.

    Sources indicate that sure, chip demand often runs in cycles, so a chipmaker arguably deserves a lower valuation multiple than a business with steadier demand. But at about 20 times expected earnings, I think a lot of that risk is already in the price.

    Sources indicate that much of the fall followed the Lumentum news, and it's clear why. Under the deal announced on Nov. 2, Lumentum shareholders will get 4.5 Marvell shares for every share they hold, and current Marvell shareholders will have around 67% of the merged manufacturer. Each existing share will be a smaller part of a bigger business.

    NASDAQ · As of 4:00 PM ET 11/23/26.

    But management expects the deal to lift adjusted earnings per share in the first year after closing, and it sees a path to over $1 billion in yearly cost savings. And Marvell expects to close the deal sometime in the first half of calendar 2028, so those new shares are probably more than a year off.

    Sure, a deal this major can go wrong, and AI spending by Marvell's largest customers could slow before it closes.

    But the data center business keeps accelerating, and the stock trades close to a market-average price for its expected earnings. I think around 20 times earnings is a good price for a manufacturer growing so fast.

    I'd buy Marvell stock here. With the stock swinging this hard from one day to the next, though, I'd space my buying out over the next several months.

    • Industry observers note that even for a large and successful firm, it's never easy to maintain a dividend, let alone increase it on a regular basis.

    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    By Eric Volkman – Nov 24, 2026 at 5:58AM EST.

    10 stocks we like better than Coca-Cola ›.

    Industry observers note that even for a large and successful firm, it's never easy to maintain a dividend, let alone increase it on a regular basis. Happily for income investors -- or really, anyone who's looking for a steady source of yield -- there's a long list of stocks that pump out a constantly rising flow of dividends.

    According to recent reports, three prominent examples of this are beverage titan Coca-Cola (KO -1.14%), big pharmaceutical organization AbbVie (ABBV +0.79%), and cleaning and household products mainstay Clorox (CLX -0.59%). This trio has kept their dividend raise trains running for decades; read on for more about these ultra-steady lifters and whether their steadily increasing payouts support the buy cases for these stocks.

    Of our trio, Coca-Cola takes the crown for longest current dividend raise streak, at a tough-to-beat 64 years. Speaking of crowns, this makes it a Dividend King, i.e., one of the select few publicly traded companies that have upped their payout at least once annually for a minimum of 50 consecutive years.

    Like clockwork, this past February Coca-Cola declared its latest dividend raise, cranking it almost 4% higher to a new quarterly amount of $0.53 per share.

    In a recent development, thanks to its asset-light business model -- the manufacturer mainly sells the syrups for its beverages, generally leaving capital-intensive processes like bottling to others -- it's highly profitable. It also generates very substantial free cash flow (FCF).

    Coca-Cola also manages to grow its fundamentals in most quarters, an accomplishment given its already considerable presence and the current unpopularity of unhealthy food and drink. In its third quarter, the organization's net revenue rose by 7% to $13.4 billion, while non-GAAP (adjusted) net income rose 11% to $3.9 billion. FCF was over $4.5 billion, far more than enough to finance the under $2.3 billion in dividend payments that quarter.

    Unless the bottom falls out of demand for the world's favorite soft drink and the many other tipples in the company's portfolio -- a highly unlikely possibility -- Coca-Cola should continue to grow, and easily be able to keep raising its dividend.

    It has been revealed that the company's next distribution will occur on Dec. 15, for investors of record as of Dec. 1. It yields 2.2% at the most recent closing stock price.

    NYSE · As of 4:00 PM ET 11/23/26.

    Another Dividend King is AbbVie, although I have to note that this is due in part to the fact that the tech giant was spun off from fellow pharmaceutical -- and longtime dividend raiser -- Abbott Laboratories (ABT +0.31%).

    Industry observers note that regardless, AbbVie is all too happy to inherit its throne and stay there. At the end of October, it confirmed a 5% dividend raise to a quarterly $1.82 per share.

    AbbVie has generally been a popular stock this year, not least because it has a strong commercial portfolio anchored by the twin blockbuster drugs Skyrizi and Rinvoq. And one fading blockbuster also in the company's immunology lineup, Humira, still generated sales of $683 million in its third quarter.

    Industry observers note that in its commercial portfolio and across numerous development programs, AbbVie is admirably diversified in important therapeutic areas (although immunology still accounts for over half of total sales). It currently boasts an enviable collection of current and potential revenue streams.

    The only catch with AbbVie these days is that its popularity has made it expensive and dampened the dividend yield (2.4% these days). For those who don't mind paying a premium for a top firm in the sector, though, the rewards could be considerable.

    In a recent development, the first payout of AbbVie's freshly raised dividend will occur on Feb. 16, 2027, for stockholders of record as of the preceding Jan. 15.

    NYSE · As of 4:00 PM ET 11/23/26.

    Recent findings suggest that clorox is on the cusp of Dividend King status, as its raise streak reached 49 years at the end of July. It most recently increased its quarterly payout by $0.01 per share to $1.25.

    It has been revealed that clorox might be trying to save a little coin because of the expense of its latest acquisition -- Gojo, the firm best known for the Purell line of sanitizers. The deal, which was announced in January and closed in April, had a net price tag of more than $1.9 billion after expected tax benefits.

    That's a significant swallow for Clorox, as its latest annual revenue figure was $6.7 billion, and in the quarter before the announcement it had only $227 million in cash.

    Recent findings suggest that the absorption of Gojo was a major factor in Clorox's 33% year-over-year rise in net sales in the first quarter of fiscal 2027, and the 82% pop in adjusted earnings per share. A low basis for comparison with the weak year-ago quarter also helped.

    According to recent reports, the Gojo deal, although it's sensible and complementary to Clorox's business, feels like a grow-by-acquisition move for a company focused on relatively mature product categories. So far this year, it's struggled with higher transportation costs and commodity prices, and those factors remain in effect. The Gojo addition notwithstanding, I don't foresee many potentially high-growth catalysts for this stock.

    That said, Clorox's beaten-down price could be attractive to bargain-hunting income investors, as its current dividend yield is a lofty 4.8%.

    Recent findings suggest that the tech giant's next dividend distribution will take place on Feb. 12, 2027, to investors of record as of Jan. 27, 2027.

    NYSE · As of 4:00 PM ET 11/23/26.
